words.e: From Etruscan letter 𐌏 (o), from Ancient Greek letter ο (o, “omicron”), derived from the Phoenician letter 𐤏 (ʿ, “ayin”), from the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓁹.

words.g: A solar or sidereal day of about 24 hours, especially (historical) Roman dates reckoned f…
words.e: Back-formed from the accusative diem (at a time when the vowel was still long), from Proto-Italic *djēm, the accusative of *djous, from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws (“heaven, sky”). The original nominative survives as *diūs in two fossilised phrases: mē diūs fidius (an interjection) and nū diūs terti…

words.g: The ninth letter of the Latin alphabet, called ī and written in the Latin script.
The name of the letter B.
words.e: Derived from Etruscan. Etruscan names of stops were the stop followed by /eː/.

words.g: (in general) head or face
words.e: From Proto-Italic *ōs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃éh₁os. Cognates include Hittite 𒀀𒄿𒅖 (aiš), Sanskrit आस् (ās), Old Irish á, Old English ōr.

words.g: Israel, another name of the patriarch Jacob
words.e: Borrowed from Koine Greek Ἰσρᾱήλ (Isrāḗl), from Biblical Hebrew יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yiśrāʾēl). The spelling Istrāhēl, from Ἰστρᾱήλ (Istrāḗl), was predominant until the dissemination of Jerome’s Vulgate (5th century CE), which popularized Isrāhēl. The h was gradually lost thereafter.

words.g: the gum arabic tree (Vachellia nilotica, syn. Acacia nilotica).
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἀκακία (akakía), from ἀκή (akḗ, “point”).

words.g: a male given name of historical usage, found e.g. in St. Mauritius.
words.e: From Mauricius

words.g: one who heaps up, amasses, or hoards
words.e: accumulō (“to amass”) + -tor

words.g: citron tree
words.e: Probably via Etruscan from Ancient Greek κέδρος (kédros).

words.g: long trumpet over 1 meter in length, especially a war-trumpet
words.e: Possibly connected to tībia (“shinbone, reed-pipe”) with similarities in meaning and form.

words.g: The twenty-third letter of the Latin alphabet, written in the Latin script.
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek Χ (Kh, “chi”), which represented /ks/ in the dialects of most of the Greek mainland and Euboea.

words.g: the Sun
words.e: From Proto-Italic *s(u)wōl, from Proto-Indo-European *suh₂ṓl (*suh₂ól-s) ~ *suh₂l-és m (“the sun”), rebuilt s-stem from *súh₂el ~ *suh₂éns n (whence Sanskrit स्वर् (svar, “the sun”)), leveled from *sóh₂wl̥ ~ *suh₂éns (from *sh₂wéns via laryngeal metathesis). Alternatively from Proto-Italic *saul th…

words.g: The name of the letter L.
to speak, talk, say
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Italic *fāōr, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰéh₂ti (“to speak”). It is unclear why the verb is deponent.

words.g: neither, neither one
words.e: From ne (“not”) + uter (“either”). In the grammatical sense, a semantic loan from Koine Greek οὐδέτερος (oudéteros), from οὐδέ (oudé, “not”) + ἕτερος (héteros, “one or the other (of two)”).

words.g: that (which is) is before one (in time), more forward, in the future; anterior (as oppose…
words.e: Comparative form of lost adjective *anterus, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros. Related to ante. Alternatively, built on ante in analogy to posterior (“which comes after”).

words.g: one who ties or binds
words.e: From alligō (“to bind”) + -tor.

words.g: a barbarous word; a word which is said incorrectly
roll of bread (usually made with unsifted flour)
words.e: From torta pānis f sg (literally “a roll of bread”); either from the feminine of tortus (“twisted, folded over”) that describes the form of the bread (torta [forma]), or from turta (“type of pastry”).

words.g: to give
words.e: From Proto-Italic *didō, from Proto-Indo-European *dédeh₃ti, from the root *deh₃- (“give”). The reduplication was lost in Latin in the present tense, but is preserved in the other Italic languages. A root aorist (from Proto-Indo-European *déh₃t) is preserved in Venetic 𐌆𐌏𐌕𐌏 (doto); the other Italic…

words.g: a male given name from Ancient Greek, equivalent to English Leon
words.e: From Ancient Greek Λέων (Léōn).

words.g: One who or which does or makes something; doer, maker, performer, perpetrator, agent, pla…
words.e: From faciō (“to do, make”) + -tor (masculine agent noun suffix).

words.g: the right of the first night; droit de seigneur
there is a snake in the grass
words.e: Literally "a snake hides in the grass" (Virgil, Eclogue III, v. 93).

words.g: a kind of marine fish
words.e: From Ancient Greek βῶξ (bôx).

words.g: brine, salt water, the sea
words.e:
From Proto-Italic *sāls, from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l. The contrast between long ā in the nominative singular and short a in the oblique forms has been interpreted as an archaic ablaut pattern that may be paralleled by pār-paris, mās-maris, and lār-laris.
Cognates include Latvian sāls, Old Armen…

The third letter of the Latin alphabet, written in the Latin script, representing the sou…
The fourth letter of the Latin alphabet, written in the Latin script, representing the so…

words.e: The minuscule form derives from the majuscule Z.

words.g: the big toe
words.e: There is a relation to hallus and allex. Might be a conflation of both. The word-initial h might stem from an assumed connection with ἅλλομαι (hállomai).

words.g: a female given name
words.e: From ursa (“she-bear”) + -ula (diminutive suffix).

words.g: to speak Latin
words.e: From latīnus + -ō.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter H/h.
newly, in a new or unusual manner
words.e: From novus (“new”) + -ē (adverbial suffix).

words.g: a tree
words.e: By rhotacism from Old Latin arbōs, from Proto-Italic *arðōs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃erdʰ- (“high; to grow”), meaning "high upright plant". Cognate with arduus (“high”).

words.g: The name of the Greek letter zeta (Ζ, ζ).
words.e: From the Ancient Greek ζῆτα (zêta).

words.g: The fruit of the vine; a grape.
words.e: From Proto-Italic *oiwā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eyHw- (“a kind of tree with berries”). Cognate with Ancient Greek ὄα (óa, “Sorbus domestica”), Old Armenian այգի (aygi, “grapevine”), Proto-Germanic *ī(h)waz (“yew”), Proto-Slavic *jь̀va (“willow”).

words.g: a wind
words.e:
Inherited from Proto-Italic *wentos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wéh₁n̥ts (“blowing”), present participle of *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”).
Cognate and synonymous with English wind, Sanskrit वात॑ (vā́ta), Avestan 𐬬𐬁𐬙𐬀 (vāta), and Ancient Greek ᾰ̓είς (ăeís). See also Latin vannus, from the same PIE root.

words.g: palladium, one of perhaps several statues of Athena, as in the Iliad and Aeneid, believed…
words.e: From Ancient Greek παλλάδιον (palládion), neuter of παλλάδιος (palládios), Παλλάς (Pallás, “of Pallas”). See Pallas.

words.g: A bad species of swelling or ulcer
words.e: From Ancient Greek κηρίον (kēríon).

words.g: one who sings with another
words.e: From ad + cantor (“singer”), from canō (“sing”).

words.g: The name of the letter G.
words.e: Derived from Etruscan. Etruscan names of stops were the stop followed by /eː/.

words.g: The name of the letter C.
words.e: Derived from Etruscan. Etruscan names of stops were the stop followed by /eː/.

words.g: The name of the letter S.
The name of the Latin script letter P/p.
words.e: Derived from Etruscan. Etruscan names of stops were the stop followed by /eː/.

words.g: beacon, signal by fire
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Italic *əngʷnis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥gʷnís (“fire”). Cognate with Lithuanian ugnis, Sanskrit अग्नि (agní), Hittite 𒀀𒀝𒉌𒅖 (akniš) (an Indo-Iranian borrowing), Old Church Slavonic огнь (ognĭ) and Old Prussian ugnis.

words.g: laurel tree
words.e:
From Old Latin dacrus.
Related to Ancient Greek δάφνη (dáphnē, “laurel”), and likely borrowed there from an Aegean or Anatolian language. Together with the rare variation δαυχμός (daukhmós) and the name δαῦκος (daûkos), used for some umbelliferous plants, Beekes derives δάφνη (dáphnē) from *dakʷ-(n…

words.g: woman or female animal that has just given birth
words.e: Substantivization of the feminine of fētus (“having recently given birth”). Found in Classical Latin in senses 1 and 2.

words.g: A woman (descended) from Latium, a Latin woman
a parma; a round shield carried by the infantry and cavalry
words.e:
Perhaps a back-formation from parmula, dissimilated from palmula, from palma (“hand”), referring to the shield being handheld.
Or, borrowed from a Celtic word.

words.g: A light made of wax or tallow; tallow candle or taper.
words.e: From candeō (“shine, glitter; glow”) + -ēla.

words.g: light, source of light
words.e: From Proto-Italic *louksmən, from Proto-Indo-European *léwk-s-mn̥, derived from the root *lewk- (“bright”). By surface analysis, lū(x) + -men.

words.g: light (of the sun, stars etc.)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *lewk-
Proto-Indo-European *-s
Proto-Indo-European *léwks
Proto-Italic *louks
Latin lux
From Proto-Italic *louks, from Proto-Indo-European *léwks. Cognates include Ancient Greek λευκός (leukós, “white, blank, light, bright, clear”), Ancient Greek *λύκη (*lúkē, “li…

words.g: one hundred-, hundred-; indicates a count of one hundred items
words.e: From centum (“hundred”).

words.g: to take or bring out or forth, produce, bring to light
words.e: From prō- (“forth, forward”) + emō (“to take, acquire, buy”).

words.g: a male given name from Hebrew, equivalent to English Moses
words.e: From Ancient Greek Μωσῆς (Mōsês), from earlier Μωυσῆς (Mōusês), from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁה (mōšê). Doublet of Mō̆ȳsēs.

words.g: to remove, take away, or subtract
words.e: From dē- (“from, away from, out of”) + emō (“to acquire, obtain”).

words.g: Acheron, a river in the underworld
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek Ἀχέρων (Akhérōn), from ὁ ἄχεα ῥέων (ho ákhea rhéōn, “the stream of woe”).

words.g: drama, play
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek δρᾶμᾰ (drâmă, “an act, a theatrical act, a play”).

words.g: to take, take up, catch, assume, seize, claim, arrogate
words.e: Ultimately from Proto-Italic *emō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁em-. By surface analysis, sub + emō (“to buy, take”), with excrescent p in sūmpsī and sūmptum. According to Sihler, the term derives from earlier *susmō, from Proto-Italic *sups-(e)mō, from *emō. It is likely that this Latin term is rel…

words.g: small bedroom; bedchamber
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *kubāō
Latin cubō
Latin -i-
Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr
Proto-Indo-European *-trom
Proto-Indo-European *-tlom
Proto-Italic *-klom
Latin -culum
Latin cubiculum
From cubō (“to lie down”) + -i- + -culum.

words.g: father (male parent)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *peh₂-?
Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr
Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr
Proto-Italic *patēr
Latin pater
From Proto-Italic *patēr, from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr. As a titular suffix, shares cognate roots with Old Latin Diēspiter (“Father Jove”), Latin Iuppiter (“Jupiter”).

words.g: a bird
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Italic *awis. Cognates include Ancient Greek ἀετός (aetós), and Sanskrit वि (ví), and Albanian vito (“woodpidgeon”).

words.g: mother (female parent)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr
Proto-Italic *mātēr
Latin mater
From Proto-Italic *mātēr, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr. Cognate with Old English mōdor (English mother).

words.g: to eat
words.e:
From Proto-Italic *edō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁édti. The long vowel in some of the forms is probably due to Lachmann's law.
Cognates include Ancient Greek ἔδω (édō), Sanskrit अत्ति (átti), Hittite 𒂊𒀉𒈪 (ēdmi, “I eat”), Old English etan (English eat), Lithuanian ėsti, Welsh ysu, and Russian есть…

words.g: to go away, walk away, leave, depart
words.e: From ab- (“from, away from”) + ambulō (“walk”).

words.g: small horse
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek νᾶνος (nânos, “dwarf”).

words.g: white hair
words.e: From Proto-Italic *sniks (with oblique stem *sniɣʷ- > niv-), from Proto-Indo-European *snígʷʰs (“snow”), root noun derived from *sneygʷʰ- (“to snow”) (whence also Latin nivit, ningit, ninguit). Direct cognates include Ancient Greek νίψ (níps), Old Irish snechtae, and indirectly also Sanskrit स्नेह…

words.g: body, person (person when used to mean "human body", e.g., "on one's person")
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Italic *korpos, from Proto-Indo-European *krépos (“body”), from the root *krep-. Equivalent to the Proto-Germanic neuter noun *hrefaz (“body, torso”), whence Old High German href, Old Dutch ref, and Old English hrif (> English riff).

words.g: big toe
words.e:
Of uncertain origin.
Traditionally connected to Proto-Slavic *palьcь (“thumb”), with contamination from Latin polleō (“to be strong”) (hence pollex, not *pōlex). However, De Vaan is unconvinced, and instead prefers Meier-Brügger's derivation from a Proto-Italic *por-likʰ-s (“which is licked over”),…

words.g: nut tree
words.e: From Proto-Italic *knuks, from a root *knu- also found in Proto-Celtic *knūs (source of Irish cnó) and Proto-Germanic *hnuts (source of English nut). Based on the form of the nouns and the restriction of the root to Germanic, Celtic and Italic, it has been argued to be of non-Indo-European origin.…

words.g: cow (female cattle)
words.e: Uncertain. It could be connected with Sanskrit वशा (vaśā), perhaps suggesting a PIE form *ueḱ-éh₂. However, this theory does not explain the /a/ in the Latin form. Perhaps a Proto-Indo-European form *woḱéh₂ may also be reconstructed. However, De Vaan argues that Latin /a/ only emerged from Proto-It…

words.g: to come (to a place), come in, arrive, reach
words.e: From Proto-Italic *gʷənjō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷm̥yéti, from zero-grade of *gʷem- + *-yéti. Cognates include Sanskrit गच्छति (gácchati), Ancient Greek βαίνω (baínō), and Old English cuman (English come).

words.g: one who kills a tyrant, an assassin
words.e: tyrannus (“tyrant”) + -cīda

words.g: a comet, meteor, shooting star
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek κομήτης (komḗtēs, “long-haired; comet”), from κομᾰ́ω (komắō, “to have long hair”) + -της (-tēs, “-er”), the former from κόμη (kómē, “hair”) which itself was borrowed into Latin as coma.

words.g: a small crescent-shaped shield of Thracian design.
words.e: From Ancient Greek πέλτη (péltē).

words.g: a present, gift, especially one for a host or vice-versa.
words.e: Derived from Ancient Greek ξένῐον (xénĭon).

words.g: man (adult male human)
words.e: From Proto-Italic *wiros, from Proto-Indo-European *wiHrós. Cognates include Sanskrit वीर (vīrá), Old Prussian wijrs, Lithuanian vyras, Latvian vīrs, Old Irish fer, Old Norse verr, Ossetian ир (ir, “Ossetians”) and Old English wer (English were-; also see world).

words.g: the old; old times, ancient times, antiquity
words.e: From vetus (“old”).

words.g: to age, make old
words.e: From vetus (“old”) + -ō.

words.g: yellowish, somewhat yellow
words.e: From sub + flāvus.

words.g: blackish, somewhat black
words.e: From sub- + niger.

words.g: hymn; a song of praise
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ὕμνος (húmnos).

words.g: a worm
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *wr̥mis
Proto-Italic *wormis
Latin vermis
From Proto-Italic *wormis, from Proto-Indo-European *wr̥mis (“worm”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *wurmiz (“worm; snake”).

words.g: inability to speak as a result of bribery
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἀργυράγχη (arguránkhē, “silver-quinsy”).

words.g: to come back, return
words.e: From re- (“again, back”) + veniō (“come”).

words.g: to intervene, come between
words.e: From inter- (“between”) + veniō (“come”).

words.g: never, at no time
words.e: From ne + umquam.

words.g: the giving of the law
words.e: Univerbation of lēgis (“of the law”) + lātiō (“carrying”), abstract noun of ferō (“to bear, to carry”).

words.g: lion's skin
words.e:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek λέων (léōn)bor.
Latin leō
Borrowed from Ancient Greek λέων (léōn).

words.g: yearly, annually, every year
words.e: From quot (“as often as”) + annus (“year”).

words.g: a secret door, back door, private entrance, postern gate
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ψευδόθυρον (pseudóthuron).

words.g: a small dagger, poniard
words.e: From pūgiō + -culus.

words.g: to give out, shed, pour forth
words.e: According to De Vaan, perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *meh₂-no-, from *meh₂- (“wet, damp”), though he shows some hesitation in ascertaining this root.

words.g: A mountain
a lotus, lotus flower (especially the species Nelumbo nucifera)
words.e: Borrowed from Dravidian; compare Kannada ಕೊಮಳೆ (komaḷe, “lotus”). Related to कुवलय (kuvalaya, “water lily”), borrowed from a different Dravidian form of the same root; compare Tamil குவளை (kuvaḷai, “blue lotus”).

words.g: a tree, (especially) any tree bearing visible flowers and fruit, but also applied to any…
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥ćšás
Sanskrit वृक्ष
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥ćšás. Cognate with Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬱𐬀 (var^əša).

words.g: a tree
words.e: Thematised from वन् (ván, “tree, wood”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wán- (“tree, wood”); see the former for more. Cognate with Younger Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬥𐬁 f (vanā, “tree”), Pashto ونه (wëna, “tree”), Sogdian wn (“tree”), Middle Persian [script needed] (wan /⁠wn'⁠/, “tree”).

words.g: a cloud
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₃meygʰ-
Proto-Indo-European *-ós
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hmaygʰás
Sanskrit मे॒घ
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hmaygʰás (“cloud”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃moygʰ-ós, from *h₃meygʰ- (“fog, cloud”).
Cognate with Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬉𐬖𐬀 (maēγa, “cloud”), Persian میغ (miġ,…

words.g: kernel or seed of a fruit
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *paẓamder.?
Sanskrit फल
Uncertain. Often considered a borrowing from Dravidian, ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *paẓam (“ripe fruit”), from *paẓV- (“to ripen, become mature”) (compare Tamil பழம் (paḻam), Malayalam പഴം (paḻaṁ), Telugu పండు (paṇḍu) and Kannada ಹಣ್ಣು (ha…

words.g: name of several plants (Indigofera tinctoria, Piper longum, Rubia cordifolia (syn. Rubia…
mother
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *máHtā (“mother”), from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬨𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭 (mātar), Old Persian 𐎶𐎠𐎫𐎠 (m-a-t-a /⁠mātā⁠/), Old Armenian մայր (mayr), Ancient Greek μήτηρ (mḗtēr), Old Church Slavonic мати (mati), Latin māter, Old English mōdor (whence…

words.g: Agni, god of fire
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hagníṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hagníš, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥gʷnís. Cognate with Latin ignis, Old Church Slavonic огнь (ognĭ), ⱁⰳⱀⱐ (ognĭ).

words.g: of a coppery red color
words.e: Related to तमस् (tamas, “gloom, darkness, obscurity”), as copper is a dark-colored metal, perhaps via a Proto-Indo-European form *tm̥H-ró-, with the long ā vowel perhaps stemming from analogical influence of forms in तम् (tam).

words.g: a fish
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *mátsyas (“fish”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬯𐬌𐬌𐬀 (masiia), Persian ماهی (mâhi).

words.g: to desire, wish, long for
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂eys-
Proto-Indo-European *-sḱéti
Proto-Indo-European *h₂isḱéti
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hišćáti
Sanskrit इ॒च्छति॑
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hišćáti (“to wish”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂i-sḱé-ti, from *h₂eys- (“to wish, desire, want”). Cognate with Avest…

words.g: old age
words.e: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂-. Cognate with Ancient Greek γῆρας (gêras, “old age”).

words.g: a name of Ganges.
words.e: Vṛddhi derivative of जह्नु (jahnu) with a -ई (-ī) extention

words.g: the sun
words.e: A -य (-ya) extension of the base सूर् (sū́r), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *súHar (“sun”), from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥ (“sun”). Cognate with Ancient Greek ἥλιος (hḗlios), Latin sōl, Persian خور (xur), English sun. Also related to स्वर् (svàr, “sun”) and सूर (sū́ra, “sun”).

words.g: more than one
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Sanskrit अन्- (an-)
Proto-Indo-European *ís?
Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háykas
Proto-Indo-Aryan *Háykas
Sanskrit एक (eka)
Sanskrit अनेक
अन्- (an-, “not, a-”) + एक (eka, “one”).

words.g: land, soil, ground
words.e:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr
Proto-Indo-European *-trom
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćšáytram
Sanskrit क्षेत्र॑
From Proto-Indo-Aryan *ṭṣáytram, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćšáytram, from Proto-Indo-European *tḱéytrom. By surface analysis, क्…

words.g: the globe, Earth
words.e: From भू (bhū, “earth, land; Earth”) + गोल (gola, “circle”).

words.g: welfare, good luck, good fortune, success, prosperity, happiness (esp. conjugal felicity)
words.e: Vṛddhi derivative of सुभग (subhaga, “fortunate”) with a -य (-ya) extension.

words.g: name of several trees
words.e: Feminine form of ताल (tāla), formed with -ई (-ī).

words.g: the letter ड
words.e: From ड (ḍa) + कार (kāra).

words.g: a lamp, light
words.e: From the root दीप् (dīp, “to burn, shine, glow”) + -अ (-a, nominalizing suffix).

words.g: gold or silver obtained through mines, pits or quarries
husband
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *pótis
Proto-Indo-Iranian *pátiš
Sanskrit पति
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *pátiš, from Proto-Indo-European *pótis. Cognate with Albanian pata, Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (paⁱti), Ancient Greek πόσις (pósis), Latin potis, Lithuanian pàts.

words.g: flowing water, river
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *nadíH (“river”). Cognate with Younger Avestan 𐬀𐬥𐬀𐬌𐬜𐬍𐬨 (anaⁱδīm, “across a river”). Possibly related to Ancient Greek Νέδα (Néda, name of a river), Middle Low German Nette (name of a river).

words.g: mountain, mountain range, height, hill, rock
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *párwatas (“mountain, rock”), from Proto-Indo-European *pérwn̥-to-s (“rocky”), from *pérwr̥ (“rock”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬙𐬁 (paᵘruuatā, “mountain”), Hittite 𒁉𒂊𒊒 (pé-e-ru /⁠péru⁠/, “rock”), 𒁉𒂊𒊒𒈾𒀭𒍝 (pé-e-ru-na-an-za /⁠pérunanta⁠/, “rocky, craggy”).

words.g: a small part of anything, any single part or portion of a whole, especially a sixteenth p…
words.e: Uncertain, though probably a derivative of either Proto-Indo-European *(s)kel- (“to bend”) or *(s)kelH- (“to cut, separate”). Mayrhofer suggests a proto-form along the lines of *(s)kolH-éh₂- for the term, and compares a seemingly-obscure Serbo-Croatian prokola (“large part of a divided whole”), as…

words.g: the midspace, between earth and heaven
words.e: The first part consists of अन्तर् (antár, “between”), or possibly an alternative form *अन्तरि (antári). The origin of the second part is disputed, suggestions are: क्षि (kṣi, “to dwell”), क्षम् (kṣám, “earth”) and ईक्ष् (īkṣ, “to see”).

words.g: Lord Brahma's egg
words.e: Compound of ब्रह्म (brahma, “priest; Brahman”) + अण्ड (aṇḍa, “egg”).

words.g: yellow (color)
words.e: Derived from पीत (pīta, “yellow”).

words.g: acidity, vinegar, wood sorrel (Oxalis corniculata)
words.e: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₂h₃m-ro- (“sour”); compare Proto-Germanic *ampraz (“sour”), Latin amārus (“bitter, sharp tasting”).

words.g: the heart
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱerd-
Proto-Indo-European *ḱḗr
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰā́rd
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰŕ̥dayam
Sanskrit हृदय
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰŕ̥dayam, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱr̥d-, oblique case stem of *ḱḗr (“heart”).
Cognate with Avestan 𐬰𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬛 (zərəd); Ancient Greek κα…

words.g: the female breast (either human or animal), teat, udder
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *(p)stánas, from Proto-Indo-European *pstón-o-s (“breast”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬟𐬱𐬙𐬁𐬥𐬀 (fštāna, “breast of a woman”) and Persian پستان (pestân, “breast”), Proto-Germanic *spenô (“nipple”), Ancient Greek στήνιον (stḗnion, “breast, chest”), Irish sine (“nipple”), Lithuanian s…

words.g: a song, sacred song or poem
words.e: Feminine of गीत (gītá), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *giHtás, from Proto-Indo-European *g⁽ʷ⁾iH-tós, from *g⁽ʷ⁾eH- (“to sing, cry”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬔𐬁𐬚𐬁 (gāθā, “form of strophe, metre, namely the collections of Zarathustra's songs, the Gathas”).

words.g: summer, the hot season (from the middle of May to the middle of July)
words.e: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥h₂-sm̥h₂-ós, from *gʷreh₂- (“heavy”) + *semh₂- (“summer”). Compare समा (sámā). Also cognate with Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬨𐬀 (hama), Persian هامین (hâmin), Old English sumor (whence English summer) through the latter component.

words.g: hair (of the head), locks of hair, tresses
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *káyśas, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *káyćas ~ gáyćas. Cognate with Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬉𐬯𐬎 (gaēsu, “curls”), Middle Persian gys (gēs, “curl, locks”) (whence Persian گیس (gis), گیسو (gisu, “ringlet of hair, forelock, sidelock, curl”)), Northern Kurdish kezî (kazī), Northern Luri گؽس (gês),…

words.g: boy; child
words.e:
The origin is uncertain. Various theories have been proposed:
* Per Turner, perhaps from a "defective word family" including बण्ड (baṇḍa, “mained, defective”). Said word family is the source for various words for children, i.e. "poor simple little beings", in various Indic languages.
* A vṛddhi der…

words.g: Jagannath, one of the names of Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu
words.e: Compound of जगन् (jágan, “world”) + नाथ (nāthá, “lord”).

words.g: horse sacrifice, the Ashvamedha ritual
words.e: An oxytonic tatpurusa compound of अश्व (áśva, “horse”) and मेध (médha, “animal sacrifice”). Possible cognate with Gaulish Epomeduos (“name of a festival and a deity”).

words.g: King of Hastinapura, husband of Gandhari, and the father of the Kauravas.
words.e: Compound of धृत (dhṛtá, “held”) + राष्ट्र (rāṣtrá, “nation”).

words.g: being in a house
words.e: Related to शाला (śā́lā, “house, hall”); see there for more.

words.g: dye, colour, especially red colour
words.e: From रञ्ज् (rañj)

words.g: a pitcher, a small water jar
words.e: Of unclear origin. Has been compared to Latin alvus (“belly, bowels”) and Lithuanian eldijà (“canoe”).

words.g: a forest or wood near a village
words.e: Possibly borrowed from Dravidian; in particular, comparisons to मलय (malaya, “name of a mountain range on the west of Malabar”) have been suggested, though this is semantically suspect.

words.g: mead; any sweet liquid
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *mádʰu (“honey, wine”), from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu (“honey, wine, mead”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬜𐬎 (maδu), Ancient Greek μέθυ (méthu), Lithuanian medùs, Old Church Slavonic медъ (medŭ, “honey”), Old English medu (whence English mead).

words.g: a father
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *pHtā́ (“father”), from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr (“father”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬌𐬙𐬀𐬭 (pitar), Latin pater, Ancient Greek πᾰτήρ (pătḗr), Old Armenian հայր (hayr), Old Persian 𐎱𐎡𐎫𐎠 (p-i-t-a /⁠pitā⁠/) (whence Persian پدر (pedar)), Old English fæder (whence English father).

words.g: long (in space and time)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *delh₁gʰ-
Proto-Indo-European *dl̥h₁gʰós
Proto-Indo-Iranian *dr̥Hgʰás
Sanskrit दी॒र्घ
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dr̥Hgʰás (“long”), from Proto-Indo-European *dl̥h₁gʰós, from *delh₁gʰ-. Cognate with Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬔𐬀 (dar^əga, “long”), Old Persian 𐎭𐎼𐎥 (d-r-g /…

words.g: tongue
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *ȷ́iźʰwáH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́iȷ́ʰwáH (compare Kamkata-viri dić, Avestan 𐬵𐬌𐬰𐬎𐬎𐬁 (hizuuā), Persian زبان (zabân)), from Proto-Indo-European *dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s (whence Old Armenian լեզու (lezu), Gothic 𐍄𐌿𐌲𐌲𐍉 (tuggō), Latin lingua, Old Church Slavonic ѩзꙑкъ (językŭ), Old Prussian…

words.g: forearm, arm
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *dáwṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dáwš, from Proto-Indo-European *dóws (“arm”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬊𐬱 (daoš), Persian دوش (duš), Proto-Slavic *(paz)duxa (“bosom, armpit”), Proto-Celtic *dows(ants).

words.g: to become bad or corrupted, to be defiled or impure, to be ruined, perish
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-European *dus- (“bad”). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic дъждь (dŭždĭ).

words.g: to sleep
words.e: From the root द्रा (drā, “to sleep”).

words.g: to sleep
words.e:
From द्रा (drā) + -यति (-yati).
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *drā́yati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *drā́yati, from Proto-Indo-European *drem-. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic дрѣмати (drěmati), Ancient Greek δαρθάνω (darthánō), Latin dormiō. More details at Proto-Indo-Iranian *nidráH.

words.g: woman, wife
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gʷḗn
Proto-Indo-European *gʷénh₂s
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ǰánHs
Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-influ.
Sanskrit जनि
The sense “woman” is from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ǰánHiš, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷḗn (“woman”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬘𐬇𐬥𐬌 (jə̄ni), 𐬘𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬌 (jaⁱni, “woman”), P…

words.g: flesh, meat
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *mems-
Proto-Indo-European *mḗmsder.
Proto-Indo-Iranian *māmsám
Sanskrit मांस
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *māmsám, from Proto-Indo-European *mēms-ó-m (“flesh, meat”). Cognate with Albanian mish, Old Church Slavonic мѧсо (męso), Latin membrum, Old Armenian միս (mis), G…

words.g: a stone, a rock
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *Háśmā, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háćmā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éḱmō. Cognate with Avestan 𐬀𐬯𐬨𐬀𐬥 (asman), Old Persian 𐎠𐎿𐎶𐎠𐎴𐎶 (asmānam), Ancient Greek ἄκμων (ákmōn), Lithuanian akmuo, Persian آسمان (âsemân).

words.g: to burn, burn down
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *Háwṣati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háwšati, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éws-e-ti, from *h₁ews- (“to burn”). Cognate with Ancient Greek εὕω (heúō), Latin ūrō.

words.g: a bone
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁
Proto-Indo-Iranian *HástʰH
Sanskrit अस्थि॑
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *HástʰH, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁. Cognate with Ancient Greek ὀστέον (ostéon), Latin os, Avestan 𐬀𐬯𐬙 (ast), Persian است (ast), Old Armenian ոսկր (oskr).

words.g: the number two
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-
Proto-Indo-European *-s
Proto-Indo-European *h₃ókʷs
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hákši
Sanskrit अक्षि
From Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hákṣi, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hákši, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ókʷs (“eye”), from *h₃ekʷ-. Cognate with Latin oculus, Ancient Greek ὄσσε…

words.g: yellow or green
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *źʰárHiṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰárHiš, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰólh₃-i-s, from *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌 (zaⁱri), Persian زر (zar, “gold”). Related to हिरण्य (híraṇya).

words.g: winter, the cold season
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰey-
Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeyméns
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰaymantás
Sanskrit हेमन्त
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰaymantás, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeyméns, from *ǵʰey- (“winter”). Cognate with Latin hībernum (“winter”), Ancient Greek χεῖμᾰ (kheîmă), P…

words.g: the hand
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰes-der.
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰástas
Sanskrit हस्त
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰástas, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰes-.
Cognate with Old Persian 𐎭𐎿𐎫 (d-s-t /⁠dasta⁠/) (whence modern Persian دست (dast)), Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬯𐬙𐬀 (zasta, “hand”), Ancient Greek χείρ…

words.g: (traditional translation) a stone for pressing out the Soma juice
words.e:
From Proto-Indo-European *gʷréh₂wō (“heavy stone”). Cognate with English quern, Old Irish brao.
It has been suggested that the word used in the Rigveda is unrelated to the sense "stone" and rather refers to a human person, meaning "praiser, singer", possibly deriving from the root गॄ (gṝ).

words.g: a tooth
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₃ed-
Proto-Indo-European *-ónts
Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hdánts
Sanskrit दत्
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hdánts, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts, from *h₃ed- + *-ónts. Cognate with Persian دندان (dandân), Ancient Greek ὀδών (odṓn…

words.g: to live
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁es-
Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésti
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hásti
Sanskrit अस्ति॑
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hásti, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésti, from *h₁es-.
Cognate with Ancient Greek ἐστί (estí), Latin est, Old Persian 𐎠𐎿𐎫𐎡𐎹 (a-s-t-i-y /⁠astiy⁠/), Hittit…

words.g: "The Vivifier"; the name of a Vedic solar deity described as the personification of the d…
words.e: From the full-grade of the root सू (sū, “to impel, to vivify”) + -तृ (-tṛ, agentive suffix).

words.g: a rock
lustre, brightness, light
words.e: प्र- (pra-) + काश (kāśa), from the root काश् (kāś).

words.g: water (also personified as a deity)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂ep-der.
Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hā́ps
Sanskrit अप्
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hā́ps, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ṓp-s ~ *h₂ép-s, from *h₂ep-..
Cognate with Avestan 𐬀𐬞 (ap), Old Persian 𐎠𐎱𐎡𐎹𐎠 (a-p-i-y-a /⁠apiyā⁠/, “into the water”), Tocharian B āp (“water”), Hittite 𒄩…

words.g: the moon
the nose
the liver
words.e:
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *yákr̥ (“liver”), from Proto-Indo-European *yókʷr̥ (“liver”).
Cognate with Avestan 𐬫𐬁𐬐𐬀𐬭𐬆 (yākar^ə), Persian جگر (jegar), Latin iecur, Ancient Greek ἧπαρ (hêpar), Old Armenian լեարդ (leard).

words.g: young ram
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥Hánas, from Proto-Indo-European *wr̥h₁ḗn (“ram”). Cognate with Ancient Greek ἀρήν (arḗn), Old Armenian գառն (gaṙn), Persian بره (barra).

words.g: woman, wife
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnā́riH (“woman”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬥𐬁𐬌𐬭𐬍 (nāⁱrī, “woman”), Middle Persian n'(y)lyk' (nārīg, “woman, lady wife”).

words.g: a wife
words.e: Exact origin obscure, but ultimately from either Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁- (“to beget, produce”) (thus literally “one who begets”) or *ǵemH- (“to marry”).

words.g: a female cat
words.e: From बिडाल (biḍāla, “cat”) + -ई (-ī, feminine suffix).

words.g: wild cat
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₃merǵ-
Sanskrit मृज् (mṛj)?
Sanskrit मार्जार
Unknown. Traditionally said to be from the root मृज् (mṛj, “to wipe”), but that is certainly a folk etymology.

words.g: milk, thickened milk
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšiHrám
Proto-Indo-Aryan *kṣiHrám
Sanskrit क्षीर
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *kṣiHrám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšiHrám (“milk”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬑𐬱𐬎𐬎𐬌𐬛- (xšuuid-), Northern Kurdish şîr, Persian شیر (šir), Zazaki şıd, şıt. Originally thought to be from Pr…

words.g: a large black bee, a kind of bumblebee, any bee
words.e:
From the root भ्रम् (bhram, “to wander”) + -अर (-ara)
Related to Ashkun bamā (“hornet”), Waigali bramā (“hornet”).

words.g: the soul
words.e: From अन्तर (antara) + आत्मन् (ātman).

words.g: breast
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *bʰúȷ́as, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰúǰas, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewgʰ- (“to bend”). Cognate with Old English būgan (whence English bow). The Sanskrit root is भुज् (bhuj).

words.g: god of the winds, a form of Vayu
words.e: From a derivative of *h₂enh₁- (“breathe”) (see अन् (an, “to breathe”)). Compare Ancient Greek ἄνεμος (ánemos, “wind, breeze”), Old Armenian անձն (anjn, “person”) and հողմ (hołm, “wind”), Old Frisian omma (“breath”), Latin animus, anima.

words.g: "purifier", wind or the god of wind, breeze, air
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *pawHanas, from Proto-Indo-European *pewH-e-nos, from *pewH- (“to be pure, clean”).

words.g: wind, air, the god of wind
words.e: From the root मरुत् (marut).

words.g: heaven; the sky
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *dyā́wṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dyā́wš, from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws m (“sky, heaven”). Cognate with Ancient Greek Ζεύς (Zeús), Latin diēs, Hittite 𒅆𒍑 (sius).

words.g: a child, infant, the young of any animal (as a calf, puppy, etc.); also applied to young…
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *śíśHuṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćíćHuš, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱiḱh₁-ú-s, a derivative of *ḱewh₁- (“to swell, to be strong”). Compare also शाव (śāva), with the same meaning and origin; perhaps the sense of "strength" later changed to mean "growth", and even later to mean…

words.g: skin (of men, serpents etc.), hide (of goats, cows etc.)
words.e: From Proto-Indo-European *twek- (“shield, skin; to cover”). Cognate with Ancient Greek σάκος (sákos, “shield”), Hittite [script needed] (tuekkaš, “body”).

words.g: the handle or ear of a vessel
words.e:
Of uncertain origin.
Likely related to Persian کر (kar, “deaf”), and perhaps to Old Church Slavonic крънъ (krŭnŭ, “mutilated (esp. of the ears and nose)”); however, Fraenkel's presupposition that "defect of the ear" was the original meaning of the common root and that Sanskrit later developed the m…

words.g: fine or white cloth, muslin
the Devanagari letter अ
words.e: अ (a, the letter) + कार (kāra, term designating a letter or sound).

words.g: mother
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *akkader.
Sanskrit अक्का
From a Proto-Indo-European lallwort *h₂ekkeh₂, compare Latin Acca Larentia, a Roman goddess, Ancient Greek Ἀκκώ (Akkṓ, “nurse of Demeter”), ἀγάλλω (agállō, “to adorn oneself, be vain or crazy”).
Alternatively from Dravidian, ultimately from Pr…

words.g: the seventh day of a lunar month, if it falls on Sunday or Monday
at night
words.e: Genitive singular of अक्तु (aktú).

words.g: at night
words.e: instrumental plural of अक्तु (aktú).

words.g: free from alkali or factitious salt
unable to walk
words.e: Compound of अ- (a-) + ग (ga).

words.g: free from disease, healthy
words.e: अ- (a-) + गद (gada)

words.g: mountain
not heavy, light
words.e: अ- (a-, “un-”) + गुरु (guru, “heavy”).

words.g: away, off, back
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hápa, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hápa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo. Cognate with Old Persian 𐎠𐎱 (apa, “away”), Avestan 𐬀𐬞𐬀 (apa), Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀢 (a-pu), Latin ab (“from”), Proto-Germanic *ab (“away from”), Proto-Slavic *po.

words.g: female child, girl, young woman (especially one under 16 years)
words.e: Feminine of बाल m (bāla).

words.g: root of a tree

words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰa(H)inúš (“milch cow”), a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)- (“to suckle, nurse”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬉𐬥𐬎 (daēnu).

Compare also Proto-Slavic *věďa (“knowledge”).

words.g: narrow
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hánźʰuṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hánȷ́ʰuš, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énǵʰus, from *h₂enǵʰ- (“narrow, tight”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬄𐬰𐬀𐬵 (ązah), Latin angustus, Old Church Slavonic ѫзъкъ (ǫzŭkŭ). Related to अंहस् (áṃhas).

words.g: a son, child
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *putrás (“son”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“small, little, few”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬎𐬚𐬭𐬀 (puθra), Old Persian 𐎱𐎢𐏂 (p-u-ç /⁠puça⁠/, “son”), Ancient Greek παῖς (paîs, “child, son”), Latin puer (“boy”), Old English fēaw (whence English few).

words.e: Unknown; possibly a Prakritism for कक्ष (kakṣa, “girdle, zone, belt”), but this is rejected by Turner. Compare Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬱𐬀 (kaša, “ocean”).

words.e: From a Near Eastern source; compare Hittite 𒊊𒌉𒀸 (parsnaš, “leopard”), Persian پارس (pârs), پلنگ (palang), Bactrian πορλαγγο-ζινο (porlango-zino), Ancient Greek πάρδαλις (párdalis), πάρδος (párdos), παρδαλέη (pardaléē).

words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšáps, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷséps (“night”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬑𐬴𐬀𐬞 (xṣ̌ap), Old Persian 𐎧𐏁𐎱 (x-š-p /⁠xšapa⁠/) (whence Persian شب (šab)), Hittite 𒅖𒉺𒀭𒍝 (ispanza).

words.e: Possibly derived from Vedic Sanskrit श्वन् (śván, gen. sg. शुनः (śúnaḥ), nom. sg. श्वा (śvā́)).

words.g: elevated, high
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hr̥šwás, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃r̥s-wó-s, ultimately from the root *h₃er- (“to rise”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬱𐬬𐬀 (ər^əšva), Ancient Greek ὄρος (óros).

words.g: widow; woman whose husband has died
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *HwidʰáwaH (“widow”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁widʰéwh₂ (“widow”). Cognate with Latin vidua, Ancient Greek ἠΐθεος (ēḯtheos), Russian вдова (vdova), Old English widuwe (whence English widow).

words.g: the act of dying; death
words.e: From मृ (mṛ, “to die”, root) + -अन (-ana, nominalization suffix) with guṇa and sandhi.

words.g: name of a fish (=कुचिक (kucika))
words.e: Of unclear origin. Perhaps from कुच् (kuc, “to bend, to draw together”), itself perhaps connected to Proto-Indo-European *kewk- (“to curve, bend”), whence German Höcker (“hump”).

words.g: earth, soil, ground; Earth personified as Bhumi
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰúHmiš (“earth”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to be”). Cognate to Avestan 𐬠𐬏𐬨𐬌 (būmi), Old Persian 𐏏 (BU /⁠būmiš⁠/) (whence Persian بوم (bum)). The Sanskrit root is भू (bhū).

words.e: From Proto-Italic *alβos, from Proto-Indo-European *albʰós. Cognates include Umbrian 𐌀𐌋𐌚𐌖 (alfu), Ancient Greek ἀλφός (alphós, “whiteness, white leprosy”), Hittite 𒀠𒉺𒀸 (alpas, “cloud”), Middle Welsh elbid (“world”), English elf, and Russian ле́бедь (lébedʹ, “swan”).

words.g: spirit
words.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ψῡχή (psūkhḗ, “soul, breath”).

words.e: From Proto-Italic *dents, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts. Cognates include Ancient Greek ὀδούς (odoús), Sanskrit दत् (dát), Lithuanian danti̇̀s, Old English tōþ (English tooth), Armenian ատամ (atam).

From Proto-Italic *nōmn̥, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥ (“name”). The long ō (and spurious g in compounds) is from false association with gnōscō (“know, recognize”). In the grammatical sense of “noun”, it is a semantic loan from Ancient Greek ὄνομα (ónoma).

words.g: big toe, hallux
words.e: From Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hangúštʰas (“thumb, big toe”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eng- (“joint”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬀𐬧𐬔𐬎𐬱𐬙𐬀 (aṇgušta), Middle Persian ʾngwst' (angust) (whence Persian انگشت (angošt)). Also related to अङ्गुरि (aṅgúri), अङ्गुलि (aṅgúli), अङ्ग (aṅgá).

words.g: a number of companions
words.e: सहाय (sahāya, “companion”) + -ता (-tā, “abstract feminine suffix”).

words.g: to stand, station oneself, take up a position on

From Proto-Indo-Iranian *staH-, from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”).
Cognates include Polish stać (literally, “to stand”), Russian стать (statʹ), Bulgarian ста́на (stána) (literally, “to stand”, compare with the Polish word), Latin stō, Ancient Greek ἵστημι (hístēmi), Old English standan…

words.e: Inherited from Middle Persian tn' (tan), from Old Persian 𐎫𐎵𐎢𐏁 (tanūš), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tanúHs, from Proto-Indo-European *tenuh₂- (“body”).

words.g: to fall
to live
to live
words.e:
From Proto-Iranian *ǰáyHati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ǰáyHati, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷéyh₃eti (“to live”), from the root *gʷeyh₃-.
Cognate with Avestan 𐬘𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (juuaⁱti), Northern Kurdish jîyan, Pashto ژوند کول (žwënd kawël), Sanskrit जीवति (jīvati). More distantly related to Ancient Greek βεί…

words.g: to play
negative; bad
words.e: Borrowed from Arabic مَنْفِيّ (manfiyy).

words.g: soft drink
words.e: By surface analysis, نوش (nuš, “ambrosia, nectar”) + آب (âb, “water”) + ـه (-e, “noun-forming suffix”)

words.g: to drink
words.e: From نوش (nōš /nuš, “wholesome drink; ambrosia”) + ـیدن (-īdan /-idan, verb-deriving suffix).

words.g: person
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Semitic *ʔadam-
Biblical Hebrew אָדָם (āḏā́m)bor.
Arabic آدَم (ʔādam)bor.
Persian آدم
Borrowed from Arabic آدَم (ʔādam), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew אָדָם (āḏā́m), from Proto-Semitic *ʔadam-.

words.g: iron (metal)
words.e: From Middle Persian [script needed] (ʾh(y)n' /⁠āhan⁠/, “iron”), from Proto-Iranian *Hácwā.

words.g: small garden, front garden/front yard
words.e: From باغ (bāġ /bâġ, “garden”) + ـچه (-ča /-če).

words.g: bone (anatomy)
words.e:
Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (ʾsthwʾn' /⁠astuxwān⁠/, “bone”), from Proto-Iranian *HástHáhuānām, a compound from *HástH (“bone”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁ (“bone”).
Cognate with Mazanderani هسکا (hassekā), Ancient Greek ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”), Latin os.

words.g: back (posterior part of the body)
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Iranian *pr̥štáh (“back”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬭𐬱𐬙𐬀 (paršta), Sanskrit पृष्ठ (pṛṣṭha).

words.g: androgenic hair
words.e: From Proto-Iranian *pášma, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *páćšma (“hair, bristles”), from Proto-Indo-European *poḱ-s-mn̥ (“hair, whiskers”), from *peḱ- (“to shear, pluck”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬱𐬨𐬀𐬥 (pašman), Sanskrit पक्ष्मन् (pakṣman).

words.g: light brown
words.e: From شن (šen, “sand”) + ـی (-i).

words.g: ice cream
words.e: From بستن (bastan, “to bind, to freeze”) + ـی (-i). Compare Turkish dondurma (“ice cream”) from dondurmak (“to freeze”).

words.g: little man
words.e: From مردم (mardom) + ـک (-ak).

words.g: to wet
to wet

words.e:
From Middle Persian 𐭰𐭲 (čat, sad), from Old Persian *θatam, from Proto-Iranian *catám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćatám, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm. Compare Northern Kurdish sed, Pashto سل (səl), Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀 (sata), Sanskrit शत (śatá), and Finnish sata.
The spelling with ص was probably introdu…

words.g: the Lord, God
words.e: Borrowed from Arabic رَبّ (rabb).

words.g: to work
to sleep; to fall asleep
words.e: From خواب (xâb, “sleep”) + ـیدن (-idan, verb-deriving suffix).

words.g: to sleep
to dream
to fly
words.e:
From Middle Persian 𐭯𐭫𐭣𐭭𐭠 (pldn' /⁠parrīdan⁠/, “fly”), from Proto-Indo-European *prew- (“to jump”).
Cognates with Northern Kurdish firîn, Central Kurdish فْڕین (firrîn), Zazaki perayen, Baluchi پرگ (parrag, “to fly away, jump off”).
Other Indo-European cognates include Sanskrit प्रवते (pravate, “to…

words.g: to swim
sustenance, daily bread
words.e: From Middle Persian lwcyk' (rōzīg, “daily bread, sustenance”), from 𐭩𐭥𐭬 (rōz [YWM], “day”). Compare Old Armenian ռոճիկ (ṙočik), Old Georgian როჭი (roč̣i), როჭიკი (roč̣iḳi), Classical Syriac ܪܘܙܝܩܐ (rōzīqā), ܪܙܩܐ (rezqā), Arabic رِزْق (rizq), all Iranian borrowings.

words.g: countryside area where people go to escape the summer heat
words.e: Of Turkic origin. Compare Azerbaijani yaylaq, Turkish yaylak, Uzbek yaylov, Kazakh жайлау (jailau), etc...

words.g: one (The first mentioned of two things or people, as opposed to the other.)
words.e: From یک (yak /yek, “one”) + ـی (-ē /-i, indefinite suffix).

words.g: two hundred
words.e: Inherited from Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠duwēst⁠/), from Avestan 𐬛𐬎𐬎𐬈𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬈 (duuesate). Cognate with Sogdian [script needed] (dwyst). Displaced by دوصد (do-sad) in eastern dialects of Persian.

words.g: deep (literal, figurative)
words.e: Borrowed from Arabic عَمِيق (ʕamīq).

words.g: cold (of temperature)
words.e: From Middle Persian slt' (/⁠sard⁠/, “cold”).

words.g: little, small (in physical size)
words.e: From Middle Persian [script needed] (hwlt' /⁠xwurd⁠/, “little”), perhaps originally the past participle of [script needed] (hwltn' /⁠xwardan⁠/, “to eat”); for the semantic development, compare the derivation of Proto-West Germanic *biti (“bit”) from *bītan (“to bite”). Compare Talysh هرد (hərd), No…

words.g: a word for time:
words.e: From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gʾs), 𐫃𐫀𐫍 (gʾh /⁠gāh⁠/, “place, throne, bed; time”), from Old Persian [script needed] (gāθu-, “place; throne, chair”), from Proto-Iranian *gātu- / *gāθu-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-European *gʷem- (“to step”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬔𐬁…

words.g: to name
words.e: From نام (nâm, “name”) + ـیدن (-idan, verb-deriving suffix).

words.g: bone (part of skeleton)
words.e:
From Ancient Greek ὀστέον (ostéon), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃esth₁-, *h₃osth₁-.
Compare Mariupol Greek студъ (stuð).

words.g: dog (Canis lupus familiaris) (general term for both sexes or more specifically, a male)
words.e: From Byzantine Greek and Koine Greek σκύλος (skúlos), from a root σκυλ- (skul-) also found in Ancient Greek σκύλαξ (skúlax, “puppy, whelp”) + -ος (-os).

words.g: two (playing card)
words.e:
From Ancient Greek δύο (dúo), from Proto-Hellenic *dúwo, from Proto-Indo-European *duwó, *duwéh₃ (*dwóh₁).
Compare Mariupol Greek дъы́я (ðýja), дъи́я (ðíja).

words.g: sun (star that the Earth orbits)
words.e:
From Ancient Greek ἥλιος (hḗlios, “sun, sunlight”), from Proto-Hellenic *hāwélios, from a pre-Hellenic or later Proto-Indo-European *sāwélios, from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥.
Cognate with Mariupol Greek и́люс (íljus).

words.g: old cow
words.e: From Ancient Greek κάμηλος (kámēlos).

words.g: red deer (Cervus elaphus)
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἐλάφιον (eláphion), diminutive of ἔλαφος (élaphos).

words.g: The lower case letter pi (πι), the 16th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter sigma (σίγμα), the 18th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
arm (portion of the upper human appendage from the shoulder to the wrist)
words.e: Inherited from Byzantine Greek χέριν (khérin), from Koine Greek χέριον (khérion), diminutive of Ancient Greek χείρ (kheír), from Proto-Hellenic *kʰéhər, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰésōr (“hand”). Doublet of χειρ (cheir).

words.g: sea (all the seas and oceans)
words.e: From Ancient Greek θάλασσα (thálassa). Cognate with Tsakonian θάσσα (thássa, “sea”), Mariupol Greek тъа́ласа (θálasa).

words.g: shallow, not deep (of water, vessel, etc)
words.e: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀβαθής (abathḗs). By surface analysis, α- (a-, “not, un-”) + βαθύς (vathýs, “deep”).

words.g: bud, eye (of a plant's shoot or flower)
words.e: From Ancient Greek ὀφθαλμός (ophthalmós).

words.g: young monk
words.e: From καλόγερος (kalógeros) + -πουλο (-poulo, diminutive).

words.g: letter (written or printed symbol)
words.e: From Ancient Greek γράμμα (grámma). Morphologically γράφω (gráfo, “to write”) + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

words.g: star (generally, any small dot in the night sky)
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek ἄστρον (ástron). The figurative sense of "fate" since Mediaeval times. The contemporary terms of the emblem or geometrical shape, semantic loan from French étoile. For "Star Wars", semantic loan from English Star Wars

words.g: breast (mammary gland)
words.e: From Ancient Greek μαστός (mastós).

words.g: The upper case letter omega (ωμέγα (oméga)), the last letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
skin (of human or animal)
words.e: From Ancient Greek δέρμα (dérma, “skin”), from δέρω (dérō, “to flay”).

words.g: mother
words.e: From Ancient Greek μήτηρ (mḗtēr, “mother”), from Proto-Hellenic *mā́tēr, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr.

words.g: love (affection, liking, attraction)
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἀγάπη (agápē). Compare Mariupol Greek ага́п (aháp).

words.g: a fat woman
words.e: From Byzantine Greek ἀγελάδα (ageláda), from the singular accusative of rare Koine Greek ἀγελάς (agelás, “grazing with the herd”), from ἀγέλη (agélē, “herd”).

words.g: beta, the second letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek βῆτᾰ (bêtă).

words.g: alpha, the name for the first letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek ἄλφα (álpha), ultimately from Phoenician 𐤀𐤋𐤐 (ʾlp /⁠ʾālep⁠/, “bull, ox”).

words.g: The upper case letter gamma (γάμα or γάμμα), the third letter of the modern Greek alphabe…
words.e: Derived from the Phoenician letter Gimel .

words.g: gamma, the third letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek γάμμα (gámma).

words.g: delta, the fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek δέλτᾰ (déltă).

words.g: The lower case letter theta (θήτα), the eighth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter iota, the ninth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter kappa (κάπα), the tenth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter lambda (λάμδα), the eleventh letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter mu (μι), the twelfth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter xi (ξι), the 14th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The lower case letter rho (ρο), the 17th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The lower case letter tau (ταυ), the 19th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The lower case letter upsilon (ύψιλον), the 20th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.

The lower case letter chi (χι (chi)), the 22nd letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
The upper case letter psi (ψι (psi)), the 23rd letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
epsilon, the fifth letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἒ ψιλόν (è psilón), further from ἔ (é) + neuter of ψιλός (psilós, “simple”). Thus, “simple e”, in contrast with αι (ai), which had become identical in pronunciation by the Koine period.

words.g: zeta, the sixth letter of the modern Greek alphabet, transliterated as Z.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ζῆτᾰ (zêtă).

words.g: eta, the seventh letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἦτᾰ (êtă), from ἧτᾰ (hêtă).

words.g: Theta, the 8th letter of the modern Greek alphabet (majuscule Θ, minuscule θ), originally…
words.e: From Ancient Greek θῆτᾰ (thêtă).

words.g: iota; the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἰῶτα (iôta), from the same Semitic source as English yodh, namely Proto-Semitic *yad- (“hand”).

words.g: lambda, the 11th letter of the Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek λᾰ́βδᾰ (lắbdă).

words.g: mu, the 12th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek μῦ (mû).

words.g: nu, the 13th letter of the modern Greek alphabet
words.e: From Ancient Greek νῦ (nû).

words.g: xi, the name for the 14th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ξεῖ (xeî).

words.g: omicron, the 15th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Koine Greek ὂ μικρόν (ò mikrón, “small O”), in contrast to ὦ μέγα (ô méga, “big O, omega”). It took its name from the round shape of the Phoenician letter 𐤏 ayin, not from its name (like other letters: e.g. άλφα (álfa) / ἄλφα (álpha) from aleph, βήτα (víta) / βῆτα (bêta) from beth, etc.)

words.g: Letter pi
words.e: From the Ancient Greek πεῖ (peî, “pi”).

words.g: rho, the 17th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ῥῶ (rhô).

words.g: sigma, the 18th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek σῖγμᾰ (sîgmă).

words.g: tau, the 19th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ταῦ (taû).

words.g: upsilon, the 20th letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ὖ ψῑλόν (û psīlón).

words.g: phi, the 21st letter of the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek φεῖ (pheî).

words.g: chi, the 22nd letter in the modern Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek χεῖ (kheî).

words.g: omega, the 24th letter of the Greek alphabet.
words.e: From Ancient Greek ὦ μέγα (ô méga). See μέγα (méga).

words.g: The lower case letter sigma (σίγμα τελικό (sígma telikó)) of the Greek alphabet when used…

Inherited from Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos), from Proto-Indo-European *drem- + Ancient Greek -ος (-os)..

words.g: god (supreme being or a supernatural, typically immortal, being with superior powers)
words.e: From Ancient Greek θεός (theós).

words.g: a female given name from Hebrew, equivalent to English Mary or Maria
words.e: Inherited from Koine Greek Μαρία (María)

words.g: God the Father
words.e: Learnedly, from Ancient Greek πᾰτήρ (pătḗr). Doublet of πατέρας (patéras).

words.g: word (word of honour)
words.e: From Ancient Greek λόγος (lógos).

words.g: rock, stone (mass or fragments)
words.e:
From Ancient Greek πέτρα (pétra).
Cognate with Mariupol Greek пе́тра (pjétra).

words.g: seed (of a plant)
words.e: From Ancient Greek σπόρος (spóros).

words.g: person
words.e: From Ancient Greek στόμα (stóma), from Proto-Indo-European *stomn̥, *stomen- (“mouth, muzzle”).

words.g: soul, spirit (essence of a person (or place or thing figuratively) usually thought to con…
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek ψῡχή.

words.g: maker: see the ancient ποιητής (poiētḗs)
words.e: Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ποιητής (poiētḗs, “maker”).

words.g: time (with no plural)
words.e: From Ancient Greek χρόνος (khrónos).

words.g: to drink (water, coffee, beers, etc)
words.e: From Ancient Greek πῑ́νω (pī́nō).

words.g: world, earth (planet)
words.e: From Ancient Greek γῆ (gê) / γαῖα (gaîa), other details uncertain.

words.g: Daniel, a book of the Bible.
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek Δᾱνῑήλ (Dānīḗl), from Biblical Hebrew דָּנִיֵּאל (Dāniyyêl).

words.g: friend

Proto-Indo-European *bʰil-o-s
Ancient Greek φῐ́λος (phĭ́los)
Greek φίλος
Inherited from Ancient Greek φῐ́λος (phĭ́los), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰil-o-s.

words.g: long established, old, former, not modern, worn out
to give birth, beget
words.e: From modern γενν(ώ) + -άω (-áo). Inherited from Ancient Greek γεννῶ (gennô), contracted form of γεννάω (gennáō). Also see γένος (génos), γενέτης (genétēs), γόνος (gónos) and the Proto-Indo-European root ǵenh₁.

words.g: to sample, take a sample
deep (downward or sometimes inward)
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek βαθύς (bathús).

words.g: sweet in taste
words.e: Inherited from the medieval γλυκός (glukós), from Ancient Greek γλυκύς (glukús, “sweet”) with metaplasm of ending as in adjectives in -ός (-ós). Compare to the formal modern usage of γλυκύς (glykýs).

words.g: son, male child
words.e: Inherited from Byzantine Greek γιός (giós) < ὑγιός (hugiós) with deletion of the unstressed vowel, from Ancient Greek υἱός (huiós, “son, child”) (see its Koine pronunciation).

words.g: when introducing a new proposal : as well is
words.e: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek γάρ (gár).

words.g: → see κοινή (koiní) (language)

words.g: to leave, depart, go
words.e: From Ancient Greek φεύγω (pheúgō, “flee”) (the sense "leave" since mediaeval times. From Proto-Hellenic *pʰéugō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewg-. Has been displaced by δραπετεύω (drapetévo) in the Ancient Greek sense of "to flee".

words.g: the majority; most people
self-seeker, selfish person (person who calculates before acting)
words.e: Calque of French calculateur (“calculating person”), after English electronic calculator, using υπολογίζω (ypologízo, “to calculate”) + -τής (-tís).

words.g: full of, loaded with, plump
words.e: From Byzantine Greek γεμάτος (gemátos), γεμᾶτος (gemâtos), from Ancient Greek γέμω (gémō, “to be full of”) + -τος (-tos). See also γεμίζω (gemízo, “to fill”).

words.g: dihedral, two sided
of black (color/colour)
words.e: Inherited from Koine Greek μαῦρος (maûros), from Ancient Greek ἀμαυρός (amaurós, “dark”). Also substantivised.

words.g: of green color/colour (colour of growing foliage)
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek πράσινος (prásinos, “leek-green”), from πράσον (práson, “leek”). Displaced earlier Ancient Greek χλωρός (khlōrós).

words.g: correct, right
words.e:
Inherited from the Hellenistic Koine Greek σωστός (sōstós, “saved”). The modern meaning ("correct"), since the mediaeval period.
Verbal adjective of the ancient verb σῴζω (sōízō, “to save”), modern σώζω (sózo), hence literally "safe and sound; secure; sure, certain".

words.g: complete, full
words.e: From Ancient Greek πλήρης (plḗrēs), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁-, pleh₁-r-. Compare Latin plērus.

words.g: sea blue
words.e: From θάλασσ(α) f (thálass(a), “sea”) + -ής (-ís).

words.g: autumn (UK & US), fall (US) (third of the four seasons, between summer and winter)
words.e: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek φθινόπωρον (phthinópōron), from φθίνω (phthínō, “to lessen, to fall down, to wilt”) and ὀπώρ(α) f (opṓr(a), “last part of summer; fruit”) + -ον n (-on). Doublet of φτινόπωρο (ftinóporo). Also see χινόπωρο (chinóporo).

words.g: kid, young goat
words.e: Ultimately from Ottoman Turkish كچی (keçi). For further etymology, see modern Turkish keçi.

words.g: kid, young goat
words.e: From Byzantine Greek γίδιν (gídin), from Ancient Greek αἰγίδιον (aigídion, “kid, young goat”).

words.g: kid, young goat
a small child (diminutive of παιδί (paidí))
words.e: παιδ(ί) (paid(í), “child”) + -άκι (-áki, “diminutive of”)

words.g: gold (metal element)
words.e: From Ancient Greek χρυσός (khrusós, “gold”) (already Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀬𐀰 (ku-ru-so)), Semitic loan, compare with Biblical Hebrew חָרוּץ (ḥārûṣ), Akkadian 𒆬𒄀 (ḫurāṣum).

words.g: collective name for vegetables of the genus Cichorium especially chicory (a group of edib…
words.e: Inherited from Byzantine Greek ραδίκι (radíki), variant of ραδίκιον (radíkion), from Italian radicchio. The form ραδίκι (radíki) may have been borrowed from the Italian plural radicchi, taken in Greek as a singular neuter. Doublet of ραντίτσιο (rantítsio), a more recent borrowing.

words.g: a male given name from Hebrew, equivalent to English Aaron
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek Ἀαρών (Aarṓn), from Biblical Hebrew אַהֲרֹן (ʾahărōn).

words.g: Artemis, the name of a Greek goddess; the Roman equivalent is Diana.
words.e: Inherited from Ancient Greek Ἄρτεμις (Ártemis).

words.g: white (color/colour)
words.e: From Hellenistic Koine Greek ἄσπρος (áspros), from Latin asper (“rough”).

words.g: street, road, way
words.e: From Ancient Greek ὁδός (hodós).

words.g: to know (something), be aware, recognize
words.e: From Ancient Greek γνωρίζω (gnōrízō).

words.g: loquat tree
altar, high altar
water (liquid H₂O)
words.e: From Byzantine Greek νερό(ν) (neró(n)), from Koine Greek νηρόν (nērón), from νηρός (nērós, “wet, damp”), from Ancient Greek νεαρός (nearós, “young, fresh”), from the term νεαρὸν ὕδωρ (nearòn húdōr, “fresh water”). Cognate with Italiot Greek nerò, Pontic Greek νερόν (nerón). Displaced earlier Ancien…

words.g: warm, hot
words.e: From Ancient Greek ζεστός (zestós), from ζέω (zéō, “to heat”).

words.g: to love
words.e:
From the modern αγαπώ (agapó), αγαπ- + -άω, from Ancient Greek ἀγαπῶ (agapô), contracted form of ἀγαπάω (agapáō).
Compare Mariupol Greek агапу́ (ahapú).

words.g: little word
words.e: λέξη (léxi, “word”) + -ούλα (-oúla, “diminutive”)

words.g: water vole, (informally) water rat
words.e: νερό (neró, “water”) + αρουραίος (arouraíos, “rat”)

words.g: cold (literally, mainly of weather & figuratively)
