words.e: From Proto-Finnic *laiva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flawją; cognates include Estonian laev. Compare also Lithuanian lai̇̃vas (“ship”).

words.g: a young person
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *noori (“young”) (compare Estonian noor), probably from Proto-Uralic *ńëre (“moist, wet?”) (compare Northern Sami njuoras, Erzya and Moksha нар (nar, “weed, grass”), Udmurt нюр (ńur, “bog, swamp”), Northern Mansi [script needed] (ńār), Hungarian nyirkos, Tundra Nenets [script need…

words.g: old (of age)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *vanha (compare Estonian vana), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wanša (compare Komi-Zyrian важ (važ), Udmurt вуж (vuž)).

words.g: wide (having a large physical extent from side to side)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *levedä (compare Ingrian levviä, Karelian levie, Veps leved), equivalent to levä- + -eä.

words.g: long (having great length)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *pitkä, derived from Proto-Uralic *pide. The comparative, superlative and many derived forms are derived from the original stem pide-.

words.g: father (male parent; male who has sired a baby, that man relative to his children)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *icä, from Proto-Uralic *ićä. Cognate with Estonian isa, Northern Sami áhčči, Moksha оця (oća, “brother of father”), оцю (oću, “big”) (compare Finnish iso) and Hungarian ős.

words.g: black (colour)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *musta.

words.g: white (of colour)
words.e: valko- (“white”) + -inen

words.g: white, (very) light (with a white or off-white color)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *valkëda (compare Estonian valge, Karelian valkie /valgie), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlketa (compare Northern Sami vielgat, Erzya валдо (valdo), Eastern Mari волгыдо (volgydo)), from *wëlke (“light”) (compare Hungarian világ).

words.g: red (color)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *punainën, equivalent to puna (“red”) + -inen.

words.g: green (colour)
words.e:
Metathesized form of Proto-Finnic *viherä, derived by -rä from Proto-Uralic *wiša (see *viha).
Further etymology and cognates.
The metathesis -erä > -reä occurred by analogy with other adjectives with the ending -eä. For the unmetathesized form, compare viheriä (“greenish”), vihertää (“to become gr…

words.g: yellow (color)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *këltainën, equivalent to kelta (“yellow”) + -inen.

words.g: one (first mentioned of two things or people)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *ükci (compare Estonian üks), from Proto-Uralic *ükte (compare Northern Sami okta, Erzya вейке (vejke), Eastern Mari ик (ik), Udmurt одӥг (odig), Northern Mansi акв (akv), аква (akva)).

words.g: hundred
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *sata (compare Estonian sada), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëta (“hundred”) (compare Erzya сядо (śado), Northern Mansi са̄т (sāt), Hungarian száz), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćatám (compare Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀 (sata), Sanskrit शत (śatá)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm.

words.g: to sleep
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *nukkudak, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Karelian n'ukkuo, Ludian nukkuda, Northern Sami nohkkat (possibly from Finnic) and possibly Estonian tukkuma and Livonian tukkõ (compare nousta ~ Estonian tõusma). May also be related to Erzya нувсемс (nuvśems, “be nodding”).

words.g: to eat
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *söödäk (compare Estonian sööma), from Proto-Uralic *sewe- (compare Erzya сэвемс (sëvems), Udmurt сины (śiny), Northern Mansi тэ̄ӈкве (tè̄ňkve), Hungarian eszik).

words.g: to drink
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *joodak (compare Estonian jooma), from Proto-Uralic *jëxe- (compare Northern Sami juhkat, Komi-Zyrian юны (juny), Northern Mansi аюӈкве (aûňkve), Hungarian iszik, Tundra Nenets ӈэ̇рпӑсь (ŋėrpăsʹ°)).

words.g: bread (foodstuff)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *laipa (compare Estonian leib (“bread”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaibaz (compare German Laib (“loaf”), English loaf, Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌰𐌹𐍆𐍃 (hlaifs, “bread”)). Slavic words like Russian хлеб (xleb, “bread”) are likewise borrowed from Germanic.

words.g: autumn, fall (season of the year)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *süksü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sükśe. Cognates include Estonian sügis, Karelian šygyžy, Northern Sami čakča, Erzya сёксь (śokś), Hungarian ősz.

words.g: door (portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *ouvi, from Proto-Uralic *owwe.

words.g: mountain (large mass of earth and rock)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *voori, from Proto-Uralic *wëre ~ *ware (compare Udmurt выр (vyr)). Compare vaara, a Sami borrowing possibly from the same Uralic root.

words.g: cow (female of Bos primigenius taurus)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lehmä (compare Estonian lehm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lešmä (compare Erzya лишме (ľišme, “horse”)), of unknown further origin.

words.g: red fox (Vulpes vulpes)
words.e: kettää (“to skin”) + -u (or a participle), probably as a euphemism for repo and because of the importance of the fox as a skin and fur animal.

words.g: to write
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kirjoittadak. Equivalent to kirja (“book, document”) + -oittaa. Original sense “to decorate with (carved, embroidered, etc.) patterns”; the sense “to write” developed after the introduction of literacy, and is attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

words.g: to read
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lukëdak (“to count”) (compare Estonian lugema), from Proto-Uralic *luke- (“to count”) (compare Northern Sami lohkat (“to read, count”), Moksha лувомс (luvoms, “to count”), Udmurt лыдӟыны (lyddźyny, “to count, to read”), Eastern Khanty ԓө̆ӈәтта (łø̆ṇətta, “to read”) and possibly H…

words.g: point, dot, full stop, period
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *pistek (“sting, prick”). Equivalent to pistää (“to sting, prick”) + -e. Originally a synonym of pisto (“sting; prick, puncture”). First used to mean "period, full stop, dot" by Gustaf Renvall in 1826 and "point" in geometry by Wolmar Schildt in 1835; other meanings derive from th…

words.g: time (inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *aika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

words.g: digit, number (symbol for a non-negative integer: 0, 1, ..., 9)
words.e: Ultimately borrowed from Latin numerus.

words.g: to come (move nearer)
words.e:
From Proto-Finnic *tuldak (compare Estonian tulema), from Proto-Uralic *tole- (compare Eastern Mari толаш (tolaš), Tundra Nenets тось (tosʹ°)).
* (emphatic future tense marker, auxiliary): Likely Swedish influence, after Swedish komma (att) and bli.
* (to cum, orgasm): Probably a semantic loan from…

words.g: to hear (perceive through hearing)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kuuldak (compare Estonian kuulma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuwle- (compare Northern Sami gullat, Moksha кулемс (kuľems), Eastern Mari колаш (kolaš), Northern Mansi хӯлуӈкве (hūluňkve), Hungarian hall).

words.g: to take
words.e:
From Proto-Finnic *vottadak (compare Estonian võtma).
* (to do something suddenly, impulsively, usually followed by ja (“and”)): Semantic loan from Swedish ta (och) ....

words.g: to know [with elative ‘about’], be aware of (in some cases implying superficial knowledge…
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *teetädäk, derived from *tee. Equivalent to tie (“road, way”) + -tää; the original meaning seems to have been “to know the way to” (thus tiedän talon (“I know the way to the house”)) or “to lead to the way to”.

words.g: iron (metal; chemical element with the symbol Fe)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *rauta, borrowed from either Proto-Germanic *raudô (compare Old Norse rauði (“hematite”)) or Proto-Balto-Slavic [Term?] (compare Latvian rūda (“ore”)), but in either case ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ- (“red”).

words.g: gold (metal; chemical element Au)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kulta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gulþą (compare Swedish guld, German Gold, English gold). Compare Livvi kultasen. Distant doublet of kelta.

words.g: tongue (organ)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *keeli (compare Estonian keel, Karelian kieli), from Proto-Uralic *käle (compare Northern Sami giella, Erzya кель (keľ), Moksha кяль (käľ), Udmurt кыл (kyl), Eastern Khanty кӧԓ (köł), Nganasan сиәде (siədje)).

words.g: ear (organ of hearing)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *korva (compare Estonian kõrv), from Proto-Uralic.

words.g: flower (reproductive structure in angiosperms; plant with such structures)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kukka. Cognate with Ingrian kukka, Karelian kukka, Votic kukkõ and possibly Võro kukk.

words.g: neck (part of the body connecting the head and the trunk)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kakla (compare Estonian kael), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kaklas (compare Lithuanian kaklas). Distant doublet of chakra, kekri, and sykli.

words.g: sleep (state of reduced consciousness)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *uni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *une. Cognates include Erzya он (on), Western Mari ом (om).

words.g: light (low in weight; unburdened)
words.e: kev- + -yt. A similar derivative is seen in Northern Sami geahppat; other cognates include Hungarian kevés. The suffix is also seen in words like lyhyt and ohut.

words.g: heavy (having great weight)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *raskas. Related to Estonian raske, Ingrian raskas, Karelian raskas and Votic raskõz. Derived from the same root as rasea.

words.g: heavy (having great weight)
words.e: painaa (“to weigh, to press (down)”) + -va (present active participle)

words.g: short (not long: having little length)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lühüt.

words.g: good (useful for a particular purpose)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *hüvä (compare Estonian hea, Veps hüvä).

words.g: narrow (having small width)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kapëda. Cognate to Estonian kabe (“lively, brisk”).

words.g: thin (having little thickness or extent from one surface to its opposite)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *ohut (compare Estonian õhuke, Võro ohut), probably from Proto-Uralic *wokše (compare Northern Khanty [script needed] (oχəл)).

words.g: to help, assist, give assistance, lend a hand, aid
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *abuttadak, derived from *apu (“help”) (whence Finnish apu); equivalent to a(v)u- + -ttaa. Compare Estonian aitama.

words.g: to continue, keep on, go on, proceed, keep going; to resume
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *jatkadak.

words.g: to dry (out/off/up)
words.e: From kuiva + -ua.

words.g: to fly (travel through the air)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lentädäk.

words.g: to leave, go, go away, set off, take off, depart, embark, sail
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *läktedäk (compare Veps lähtta), from Proto-Uralic *läkte- (compare Skolt Sami liõhttâd, Erzya ливтемс (ľivťems, “to take away, bear”), Eastern Mari лекташ (ĺektaš, “to leave, travel”), Udmurt лыктыны (lyktyny, “to come”), Eastern Khanty [script needed] (Liɣwǝt-)).

words.g: to go [with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (move away from a point of reference)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *mendäk (compare Estonian minema, Karelian männä), from Proto-Uralic *mene- (compare Northern Sami mannat, Eastern Mari мияш (mijaš), Komi-Zyrian мунны (munny), Northern Mansi минуӈкве (minuňkve), Hungarian megy (men-), Tundra Nenets минзь (myinzʹ°)).

words.g: to laugh
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *nakradak, of unknown ultimate origin. Cognates include Estonian naerma, Karelian nakrua.

words.g: to love
words.e: rakas (“dear, beloved”) + -taa

words.g: to play (produce music using a musical instrument; use a device to hear a recording)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *soittadak. Equivalent to soida (“to make a sound, ring”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

words.g: to play (participate in (a sport or game))
words.e: peli (“game”) + -ata

words.g: bird (animal in the class Aves, having a beaked mouth and usually capable of flight)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lintu, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lunta or *linta, a cognate of Estonian lind, Ter Sami lonnˈt, Northern Mansi лунт (lunt) and Hungarian lúd.

words.g: snow (frozen, crystalline state of water that falls as precipitation; sometimes also simi…
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lumi, from Proto-Uralic *lome.

words.g: fish (aquatic animal)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kala (compare Estonian kala), from Proto-Uralic *kala (compare Northern Sami guolli, Erzya кал (kal), Eastern Mari кол (kol), Hungarian hal, Tundra Nenets халя (xalya)).

words.g: to earth, ground, ground out
words.e: maa + -taa + -oittaa; irregularly derived

words.g: cold (having a low temperature)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *külmä (compare Estonian külm), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *külmä (compare Ter Sami kallm, Erzya кельме (keľme), Eastern Mari кылме (kylme)), which is possibly an Indo-European borrowing (compare Pre-Baltic *gu̯el(u)mā, Pre-Balto-Slavic *gʷel(h₁)-mo-, both of which derive fr…

words.g: hot (having a high temperature)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kuuma.

words.g: dry (free from or lacking moisture)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kuiva (compare Estonian kuiv), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kujwa.

words.g: wet (made of liquid or moisture)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *märkä (compare Estonian märg), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian mērka (“humidity”)).

words.g: high (physically elevated, extending above a base or average level; located at a great al…
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *korkëda.

words.g: right (opposite of left)
words.e:
From Proto-Finnic *oikëda (compare Estonian õige), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wojketa (“straight”) (compare Erzya виде (viďe)).
Semantic development
* The original sense was "straight".
* "straight" → "right, correct": has parallels in other languages, e.g. Latin rēctus and English right from "straig…

words.g: left (on the left side)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *vasën, from Proto-Uralic *wasa (originally with the comparative suffix -mpi).

words.g: mouth (organ)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *suu (compare Estonian suu), from Proto-Uralic *śuwe (compare Northern Mansi сӯп (sūp), Hungarian száj, Tundra Nenets сё (syo)).

words.g: tree (large woody plant)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *puu (compare Estonian puu, Karelian puu), from Proto-Uralic *puwe / *pawe (compare Eastern Mari пу (pu), Udmurt пу (pu), Hungarian fa, Tundra Nenets пя (pya)).

words.g: abessive singular of go
to sing
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *lauladak. Cognate with Estonian laulma, Võro laulma, Northern Sami lávlut. Possibly ultimately onomatopoeic, as sounds like tra-la-la, "la-la" or similar are associated with singing in many languages.

words.g: to shoot, fire (fire a projectile or a weapon that fires a projectile)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *ampudak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ampɜ-. Probably cognate to Erzya аволдамс (avoldams, “to swing”).

words.g: to stand (be in a standing position)
words.e: seistä (“to stand”) + -oa. Cognate with Ingrian seisoa, Karelian seisuo and Ludian seižuda. See seistä for further etymology.

words.g: blood (liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *veri (compare Estonian veri, Livonian ve’r), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *were (compare Northern Sami varra, Erzya верь (veŕ), Eastern Mari вӱр (vür), Udmurt вир (vir), Hungarian vér).

words.g: eye (organ of the body)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *silmä (compare Estonian silm), from Proto-Uralic *śilmä (compare Northern Sami čalbmi, Erzya сельме (śeľme), Eastern Mari шинча (šinča), Udmurt син (śin), Northern Mansi сам (sam), Northern Khanty сєм (sêm), Hungarian szem, Tundra Nenets сэв (sew°)).

words.g: nose (protuberance on the human face)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *nenä.

words.g: letter (such of the alphabet, character, glyph)
words.e: kirjata (“to document in writing”) + -in (instrumental noun suffix). Coined by Finnish physician and translator Erik Alexander Ingman in 1834.

words.g: letter (a written message)
words.e: kirja (“book, writing”) + -e. Coined by Finnish physician and translator Wolmar Schildt in 1844; kirje had also been used some years before in the sense “letter (of the alphabet)”, which is now kirjain.

words.g: book (collection of sheets of paper bound together containing printed or written material)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *kirja. Originally meant something like "carved mark or decoration" or "embroidered decoration", and some derived terms get their meaning from these former senses (e.g. kirjonta (“embroidery”)). The modern sense developed after the introduction of writing and has developed somewha…

words.g: a male given name
words.e: From Latin Paulus, probably via Swedish Paul, German Paul or English Paul. Cognate with the older Finnish Paavo.

words.g: An alb; a long white gown worn in various Christian ceremonies by the priest or the paris…
words.e: From Latin alba.

words.g: thin, narrow strip of material; batten, fillet, strip, bead
words.e: Borrowed from Swedish list, lista.

words.g: moist, humid, damp, wet (with high humidity or some liquid, but not completely impregnate…
words.e: Equivalent to kostaa + -ea. Sense contaminated by the family of kastaa; see kostua for more.

words.g: father
words.e: Borrowed from Swedish fader (“father”).

words.g: The god of depths, water, and fishing.
words.e: Probably ahtaa + -i. The consonantism implies a relatively recent derivation, but based on the dialectal meaning "to hang up to dry". The god of water and fishing would have thus originally been a god that helps keep fish nets dry and thus by extension bring a good catch. Alternatively possibly bor…

words.g: A variation of Ahti, name of the god of the depths, water, and fishing in Finnish mytholo…
words.e: A variant of Ahti (mythology), roughly equivalent to Ahti + -o.

words.g: The letter C in the Finnish spelling alphabet.
words.e: From Swedish Celsius.

words.g: a male given name
words.e: From Biblical Hebrew שָׁאוּל (šāʾûl, literally “asked (for)”).

words.g: Milky Way (the broad band of diffuse white light, visible in the night sky)
words.e: linnun (“bird's”, genitive) + rata (“track”), named after the purported path taken by birds to spend their winter in lintukoto in Finnic folklore.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter R/r.
words.e: Ultimately from Latin er. See äs for further details on the vowel.

words.g: seed (fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant)
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *seemen, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *sḗˀmin, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₁mn̥. Doublet of hieman.

words.g: a male given name from the Germanic languages, equivalent to English Robert
words.e: From Swedish Robert, from English Robert or Latin Robertus, from Frankish *Hrōþiberht.

words.g: to burn
words.e: From Proto-Finnic *paladak, from Proto-Uralic *pala-.

words.g: The twenty-sixth letter of the Finnish alphabet, called ruotsalainen oo and written in th…
words.e: See Å.

words.g: The first letter of the Czech alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The eleventh letter of the Czech alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The thirty-ninth letter of the Czech alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The name of the Latin script letter N/n.
drink (a (mixed) alcoholic beverage)
words.e: Borrowed from English drink.

words.g: green (a putting green; the part of a golf course near the hole)
words.e: Derived from English green.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter L/l.
kiwi, kiwi fruit
words.e: Borrowed from Māori kiwi. The fruit is named after the bird.

words.g: oak, oak tree
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech dub, from Proto-Slavic *dǫbъ (“oak tree, oak”).

words.g: The fourteenth letter of the Czech alphabet, written in the Latin script; preceded by H a…
mother
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech matka, from Proto-Slavic *matъka. By surface analysis, máti + -ka.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter R/r.
short masculine singular of bledý
leaf (green and flat organ of vegetative plants)
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech list, from Proto-Slavic *listъ (“leaf”).

words.g: The eighth letter of the Czech alphabet, written in the Latin script.

a female given name
words.e: Borrowed from Latin Laura.

words.g: aha, I see (expresion of understanding, realization, invention or recognition)
kilo, short for kilogram
words.e: Clipping of kilogram.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter M/m.
The name of the Latin script letter S/s.
a male given name from Hebrew, equivalent to English Michael
words.e: From Vulgate Latin Michaēl, Michahēl, from Biblical Hebrew מִיכָאֵל (mîḵāʾēl, literally “who is like God?”).

words.g: rock (style of music)
words.e: Borrowed from English rock.

words.g: a male given name from Hebrew, equivalent to English Daniel
New York, New York City (the largest city in the state of New York, and the largest city…
words.e: Borrowed from English New York.

words.g: a male given name
boilery, boiling house
words.e: From vařit + -na.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter T/t.
hymn; a song of praise
words.e: Borrowed from Latin hymnus, borrowed from Ancient Greek ὕμνος (húmnos).

words.g: outdated word for small cattle like pigs, goats, sheep
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *borvъ.

words.g: people
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ľudъ.

words.g: back (the reverse side)
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *rǫbъ (“something which was cut”), from *rǫbati (“to cut, chop”).

words.g: day (24 hours, usually from midnight to midnight)
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech den, from Proto-Slavic *dьnь (“day”).

words.g: short masculine singular of bosý
to take off (a shoe)
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech zúti, from Proto-Slavic *jьzuti (“to take off (footwear)”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *áutei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ew-. Cognate with Latin exuere.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter Z/z.
soul (music style)
persimmon fruit
words.e: Borrowed from Japanese 柿 (kaki).

words.g: number
bastard, love child (person born to unmarried parents)
head (part of the body)
words.e: Inherited from Old Czech hlava, from Proto-Slavic *golva.

words.g: prime number
words.e: From prvý + -o- + číslo.

words.g: ice cream

Cognate with Lao ເງິນ (ngœn), Northern Thai ᨦᩮᩥ᩠ᨶ, Lü ᦇᦹᧃ (nguen), Tai Dam ꪹꪉꪷꪙ, Shan ငိုၼ်း (ngúen), Tai Nüa ᥒᥫᥢᥰ (ngöen), Phake င︀ိုꩫ︀် (ṅün), Ahom 𑜂𑜢𑜤𑜃𑜫 (ṅün), Bouyei nganz, Zhu…

words.g: light emitting from a centre: corona, aureole, halo, nimbus, etc.
words.e: From Sanskrit रश्मि (raśmi, “ray of light”). Cognate with Lao ລັດສະໝີ (lat sa mī), Northern Thai ᩁᩢᩔ᩠ᨾᩦ (lat⁶ sa mii¹), Old Khmer *raśmi, raśmiy, Modern Khmer រស្មី (rĕəʼsməy). Compare Pali raṃsi, from which Thai รังสี (rang-sǐi) is derived.

words.g: relative: a person connected by blood, marriage, or adoption.
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit जाति (jāti, “family”) or Pali ñāti (“family”).

words.g: (พระ~) Agni, the Hindu god of fire
words.e:
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit อคฺนิ (agni, “fire”). Doublet of อัคคี (àk-kii). Ultimately cognates with English ignite.
Cognate with Lao ອັກຄະນີ (ʼak kha nī).

words.g: friend
words.e: First attested in the Inscription of Wat Si Chum (จารึกวัดศรีชุม), c. 1341-1367. Possibly borrowed from Middle Khmer សហាយ (sahāya), ultimately from Sanskrit सहाय (sahāya, “friend; follower”) or Pali sahāya (“companion”).

words.g: friend
words.e: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit मित्र (mitra, “friend”). Cognates include Khmer មិត្ត (mɨt), Lao ມິດ (mit).

words.g: A letter of the Thai alphabet; it is usually regarded as a vowel.
words.e: Created to represent Sanskrit ऋ (ṛ).

words.g: A letter of the Thai alphabet; it is usually regarded as a vowel.
words.e: Created to represent Sanskrit ॠ (ṝ).

words.g: A letter of the Thai alphabet; it is usually regarded as a vowel.
words.e: Created to represent Sanskrit ऌ (ḷ).

words.g: A letter of the Thai alphabet; it is usually regarded as a vowel.
words.e: Created to represent Sanskrit ॡ (ḹ).

words.g: (พระ~) Brahma, one of the supreme gods, the creator of the universe, often depicted with…
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit ब्रह्म (brahma, “Brahma”) or Pali brahma (“idem”).

words.s: พริกขี้หนู
words.g: bird's eye chili, Capsicum annuum.
words.e: From พริก (prík, “pepper; chilli”) + ขี้ (kîi, “excrement”) + หนู (nǔu, “mouse”), literally “mouse-shit pepper”.

words.g: bell pepper; sweet pepper.
words.e: From พริก (prík, “chilli”) + หยวก (yùuak, “banana stalk”).

words.g: people
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit प्रजा (prajā́, “people”).

words.g: form; manner; means; way
words.e: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit प्रकार (prakāra, “form”). Compare Pali pakāra, whence Thai ปการ. Cognate with Lao ປະການ (pa kān), Lü ᦕᦂᦱᧃ (ṗhk̇aan).

words.g: person, people
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit जन (jana, “person”) or Pali jana (“person”). Cognate with Lao ຊົນ (son).

words.g: to move or come (towards the speaker's direction); to arrive.
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ʰmaːᴬ (“to come”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨾᩣ (maa), Khün ᨾᩣ (maa), Isan มา, Lao ມາ (mā), Lü ᦙᦱ (maa), Tai Dam ꪣꪱ, Tai Dón ꪝꪱ, Shan မႃး (máa), Tai Nüa ᥛᥣᥰ (mäa), Aiton မ︀ႃ (mā), Phake မ︀ႃ (mā), Ahom 𑜉𑜠 (ma) or 𑜉𑜡 (mā) or 𑜉𑜡𑜠 (māa), Zhuang maz.

words.g: to call: to cry out or shout.
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *riəkᴰᴸ⁴ (“to call”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩁ᩠ᨿᨠ, Khün ᩁ᩠ᨿᨠ, Isan เฮียก, Lao ຮຽກ (hīak), Lü ᦵᦣᧅ (hek), Shan ႁဵၵ်ႈ (hāek), Phake ꩭိက︀် (hik), Ahom 𑜍𑜢𑜀𑜫 (rik), Saek เหร้ก.

words.g: to search: to go through, look through, explore, examine, etc., in order to find or disco…
to yield; to give way; to give in.
words.e: Cognate with Lao ຍອມ (nyǭm), Northern Thai ᨿᩬᨾ, Khün ᨿᩬᨾ, Lü ᦍᦸᧄ (yoam), Shan ယွမ်း (yáum), Tai Nüa ᥕᥩᥛ (yoam), Ahom 𑜊𑜨𑜪 (jʸoṃ).

words.g: to know (information), to be aware
words.e: From Proto-Tai *rɯːwꟲ (“to know”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩁᩪ᩶, Isan ฮู้, Lao ຮູ້ (hū), Lü ᦣᦴᧉ (huu²), Tai Dam ꪭꪴ꫁, Shan ႁူႉ (hṵ̂u), Ahom 𑜍𑜥 (rū) or 𑜍𑜤𑜈𑜫 (ruw), Zhuang rox, Saek รอ.

words.g: to remove; to take off
words.e: Borrowed from Middle Chinese 脫 (MC dwat|thwat, “take off”). Cognate with Lao ຖອດ (thǭt), Northern Thai ᨳᩬᨯ, Lü ᦏᦸᧆᧈ (ṫhoad¹), Tai Dón ꪖꪮꪒ, Shan ထွတ်ႇ (thàut), Tai Nüa ᥗᥨᥖᥱ (thǒt), Ahom 𑜌𑜨𑜄𑜫 (thot).

words.g: to drop, fall, fall (straight) down (from, into, onto)
words.e: From Proto-Tai *tokᴰ (“to drop”). Cognate with Lao ຕົກ (tok), Lü ᦷᦎᧅ (ṫok), Shan တူၵ်း (túuk), Ahom 𑜄𑜤𑜀𑜫 (tuk), Bouyei dogt, Zhuang doek.

words.g: pine: any tree of the genus Pinus.
to follow; to come after; to go after.
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *taːmᴬ¹ (“to follow; to continue”). Cognate with Lao ຕາມ (tām), Lü ᦎᦱᧄ (ṫaam), Shan တၢမ်း (táam), Tai Nüa ᥖᥣᥛᥰ (täam).

words.g: to be or go against (a law, a requirement, one's or someone's desire, etc).
words.e: Cognate with Lao ຝຶນ (fưn) or ຝືນ (fư̄n), Northern Thai ᨺᩨ᩠ᨶ (fɯɯn¹), Khün ᨺᩨ᩠ᨶ (fɯɯn¹).

words.g: to dry (in the sun or the air)
words.e:
From Proto-Tai *p.raːkᴰ (“to expose to the sun”).
Cognate with Northern Thai ᨲᩣ᩠ᨠ, Zhuang dak and byak (dialectal).

words.g: to read
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ʔaːnᴮ (“to recite”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩋ᩵ᩣ᩠ᨶ, Lao ອ່ານ (ʼān), Tai Dam ꪮ꪿ꪱꪙ, Lü ᦀᦱᧃᧈ (˙ʼaan¹), Shan ဢၢၼ်ႇ (ʼàan), Ahom 𑜒𑜃𑜫 (ʼan), Tày án. Compare Khmer អាន (ʼaan).

words.g: to peck, as a bird does
to make eye contact.
to bind; to tie round
words.e: Borrowed from Middle Chinese 翻 (MC phjon). Cognate with Lao ພັນ (phan), Lü ᦗᧃ (pan), Shan ပၼ်း (pán).

words.g: to come down; to get down; to descend
words.e: From Proto-Tai *n̩.loŋᴬ (“to descend”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩃᩫ᩠ᨦ, Lao ລົງ (long), Lü ᦟᦳᧂ (lung), Tai Dam ꪶꪩꪉ, Shan လူင်း (lúung), Tai Nüa ᥘᥨᥒᥰ (löng), Ahom 𑜎𑜤𑜂𑜫 (luṅ), Zhuang roengz.

words.g: to scrape with a sharp object.
to hold in the mouth (for various purposes, such as for letting the thing held dissolve i…
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ʔɤmᴬ (“to hold in the mouth”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩋᩫ᩠ᨾ, Khün ᩋᩫ᩠ᨾ, Lao ອົມ (ʼom), Lü ᦷᦁᧄ (ʼom), Shan ဢူမ် (ʼǔum), Ahom 𑜒𑜤𑜉𑜫 (ʼum), Zhuang oem, Nong Zhuang umq.

words.g: to swim
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Tai *hwaiꟲ¹. Cognate with Northern Thai ᩉ᩠ᩅ᩶ᩣ᩠ᨿ, Lao ຫວ້າຍ (huāi), Lü ᦛᦻᧉ (v̇aay²), Shan ဝၢႆႈ (wāai), Nong Zhuang heuz, Zhuang vaij.

words.g: child: person below the age of adulthood.
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ɗekᴰ (“child (young person)”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨯᩮᩢ᩠ᨠ, Lao ເດັກ (dek), Saek แด๊ก, Zhuang daeg. Compare also Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *bataq.

words.g: jar, especially one of large size.
words.e: From Old Chinese 甕 (OC *qoːŋs). Cognate with Lao ໂອ່ງ (ʼōng).

words.g: Thai boy or young man of Chinese descent, especially one with stereotypical Chinese featu…
words.e: Borrowed from Teochew 弟 (di6, “younger brother”).

words.g: to take by force: to usurp, to seize, to rob, etc.
words.e: Possibly from Old Khmer plan.

words.g: (พระ~) time or point of time believed to bring good or bad outcomes, as determined by an…
words.e: From Sanskrit ऋक्ष॑ (ṛ́kṣa, “constellation; lunar mansion; star”). Cognate with Old Khmer ṛkṣa (“lunar mansion”), Khmer ឫក្ស (rɨk, “auspicious time determined by astrologer; star”).

words.g: To make one famous.
right side (opposite of left).
words.e: Borrowed from Old Chinese 右 (OC *ɢʷɯʔ, *ɢʷɯs, “right”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨡ᩠ᩅᩣ, Lao ຂວາ (khuā), Lü ᦧᦱ (ẋwaa), Shan ၶႂႃ (khwǎa), Zhuang gvaz, Bouyei gvaz. Compare Sui fal (“right”), Southern Kam wap (“right”).

words.g: mountain
words.e: ภู (puu, “mound”) + เขา (kǎo, “hill, mountain”). Cognate with Lao ພູເຂົາ (phū khao).

words.g: a female given name from Sanskrit
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit पद्म (padma, “lotus”).

words.g: good wish; blessing; benediction
words.e:
Borrowed from Old Khmer bara° (“blessing; benediction”); ultimately from Sanskrit वर (vara, “best, excellent; royal, princely; valuable, precious; boon; etc”).
Cognate with Old Khmer vara, var; Modern Khmer ពរ (pɔɔ), វរ (vɔɔ); Lao ພອນ (phǭn).
Doublet of พระ (prá) and วร (wɔɔn).

words.g: a third person pronoun: he, she, it, they, etc.
words.e: From Proto-Tai *bɯən (“friend”), from Middle Chinese 伴 (MC banX, “companion; partner”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨻᩮᩬᩥ᩵ᩁ, ᨻᩮᩥ᩠᩵ᨶ, Lao ເພື່ອນ (phư̄an), ເພິ່ນ (phœn), Shan ပိူၼ်ႈ (pōen), Vietnamese bạn.

words.g: a first person pronoun: I.
words.e:
From Proto-Tai *kuːᴬ (“I”, singular first-person pronoun (weak)), from Proto-Kra-Dai *akuː.
Cognate with Lao ກູ (kū), Lü ᦅᦴ (kuu), Tai Dam ꪀꪴ, Zhuang gou.
Compare Proto-Hlai *ɦuː (“I”), Proto-Austronesian *aku (whence Malay aku, Tagalog ako and Javanese aku).

words.g: to come into being: to be born, to rise, to originate, to emerge, to occur, to happen, to…
words.e: From Pre-Angkorian Old Khmer កេត៑ (ket), កេត្ត៑ (kett, “to bring into existence; to come into existence; etc”), which later became into Middle Khmer កេត~កើត~កេត្រ~កើត្រ (keta~kœta~ketra~kœtra), cognate with Modern Khmer កើត (kaət); extended as កំនេត (kaṃneta), កុំនេត (kuṃneta), etc, from which กำเน…

words.g: a first person pronoun employed by a male when addressing a person of equal or higher sta…
words.e: Uncertain.

words.g: a first person plural/singular pronoun employed when addressing a person of equal or lowe…
words.e: From Proto-Tai *rawᴬ (“first person plural pronoun”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩁᩮᩢᩣ, Isan เฮา, Lao ເຮົາ (hao), Lü ᦣᧁ (haw), Tai Dam ꪹꪭꪱ, Tai Nüa ᥞᥝᥰ (häw), Shan ႁဝ်း (háo), Ahom 𑜍𑜧 (raw), 𑜍𑜈𑜫 (raw) or 𑜍𑜧𑜈𑜫 (raww), Bouyei rauz, Zhuang raeuz.

words.g: a female given name from Sanskrit
words.e: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit सुमित्रा (sumitrā, literally “good friend”), from सु (su, “good”) + मित्रा (mitrā, “friend”). By surface analysis, สุ (sù) + มิตรา.

words.g: Sucitrā, one of the four chief wives of the god Indra.
words.e: From Sanskrit सुचित्रा (sucitrā), from सु (su, “easy; good, fine, excellent”) + चित्रा (citrā, “illusion; unreality; etc”), equivalent to Thai สุ (sù) + จิตรา.

words.g: a female given name from Sanskrit
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit कल्याणी (kalyāṇī, “beneficial one; beautiful one”) or Pali kalyāṇī (“idem”).

words.g: water buffalo (the animal Bubalus bubalis of the family Bovidae)
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ɣwaːjᴬ (“water buffalo”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨤ᩠ᩅᩣ᩠ᨿ, Isan ควย, Lao ຄວາຍ (khuāi), Lü ᦩᦻ (xwaay), Tai Dam ꪁꪫꪱꪥ (kwaay4), Tai Dón ꪅꪫꪱꪥ (xwaay4), Tai Daeng ꪃꪫꪱꪥ (khwaay4), Shan ၵႂၢႆး (kwáai), Tai Nüa ᥑᥣᥭᥰ (xäay), Ahom 𑜁𑜨𑜩 (khoy) or 𑜁𑜩 (khay), Zhuang vaiz, Saek ว๊าย.

words.g: wealthy person
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit श्रेष्ठी (śreṣṭhī, “merchant”). Compare Old Khmer sesṭhi (“wealthy merchant”); Modern Khmer សេដ្ឋី (seetthəy, “wealthy man”); Lao ເສດຖີ (sēt thī); Pali seṭṭhī (“wealthy man”).

words.g: air; breath; wind
words.e: Borrowed from Pali vāyu (“wind”), from Sanskrit वायु (vāyú). Cognate with Modern Khmer ព្យុះ (pyuh); Lao ພາຍຸ (ph), ວາຍຸ (w). Compare Old Khmer vyuha.

words.g: a female given name from Sanskrit
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit चिन्तन (cintana, “thinking”).

words.g: (พระ~) Candra, the moon god.
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit चन्द्र (candra, “shining; the shining one (referring to the moon)”). Cognate with Old Khmer candra, can, °cann; Modern Khmer ចន្ទ្រ (can), Lao ຈັນ (chan), Lü ᦶᦈᧃ (ṫsaen), Shan ၸၼ်ႇတႃႇ (tsàn tàa). Compare Pali canda, from which Thai จันท์ is derived.

words.g: red precious stone, as ruby.
words.e: From Pali maṇi (“precious stone; gem; jewel”) or Sanskrit मणि (maṇi, idem); probably via Old Khmer mnī, mni, *maṇi, muṇī (“precious stone; gemstone”). Cognate with Lao ມະນີ (ma nī), Northern Thai ᨾᨱᩦ, Modern Khmer មណី (mĕəʼnii).

words.g: ten thousand (Thai numerals: ๑๐๐๐๐ (10000))
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Tai *mɯn. From Middle Chinese 萬 (MC mjonH, “ten thousand”). Cognate with Old Khmer hmīna, hmï̄ṇa, hmina, hmœna (“ten thousand”); Modern Khmer ម៉ឺន (məɨn), ហ្មឺន (məɨn); Lao ໝື່ນ (mư̄n); Lü ᦖᦹᧃᧈ (ṁuen¹); Shan မိုၼ်ႇ (mùen); Vietnamese muôn.

words.g: chest, breast
words.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit उरस् (uras, “chest”).

words.g: past: time gone by; time past.
words.e: From Pali atīta (“past; gone by”), from Sanskrit अतित (atita, “idem”). Cognate with Lao ອາດີດ (ʼā dīt), Khmer អតីត (ʼaʼdət), Burmese အတိတ် (a.tit), Hindi अतीत (atīt).

words.g: that which brings good or prosperity; good or prosperity itself.
words.e: From Pali maṅgala (“good; propitious; etc”), from Sanskrit मङ्गल (maṅgala, “idem”) Cognate with Burmese မင်္ဂလာ (mangga.la); Old Khmer maṅgala, muṅgala, etc; Modern Khmer មង្គល (mŭəngkŭəl).

words.g: true seal: marine mammal of the family Phocidae.
words.e: From แมว (mɛɛo, “cat”) + น้ำ (náam, “water”); literally "water cat" or "aquatic cat".

words.g: sea lion.
words.e: Calque of English sea lion. Same as สิงโต (sǐng-dtoo, “lion”) + ทะเล (tá-lee, “sea”).

words.g: big sister, elder sister.
words.e: From พี่ (pîi) + สาว (sǎao). Cognate with Ahom 𑜆𑜣 𑜏𑜰𑜫 (Pi Sau).

words.g: big brother, elder brother.
words.e: From พี่ (pîi) + ชาย (chaai). Cognate with Ahom 𑜆𑜣 𑜋𑜩 (pi chai).

words.g: girl, young woman.
words.e: From Proto-Tai *saːwᴬ (“unmarried woman”). Cognate with Lao ສາວ (sāo), Lü ᦉᦱᧁ (ṡaaw), Tai Nüa ᥔᥣᥝᥲ (sàaw), Shan သၢဝ် (sǎao), Tai Dam ꪎꪱꪫ, Ahom 𑜏𑜧 (saw), 𑜏𑜨𑜧 (sow), 𑜏𑜧𑜤 (sawu), 𑜏𑜧𑜈𑜫 (saww), or 𑜏𑜦𑜡 (sō), Zhuang sau, Tày slao.

words.g: star (any sense)
words.e:
From Proto-Tai *t.naːwᴬ. Cognate with Lao ດາວ (dāo), Northern Thai ᨯᩣ᩠ᩅ, Lü ᦡᦱᧁ (ḋaaw), Shan လၢဝ် (lǎao), Tai Dam ꪒꪱꪫ, Tày đao, Zhuang ndaundeiq.
Compare Proto-Hlai *ɾaːw (“star”), Proto-Austronesian *qajaw (whence Paiwan qadaw (“sun, day”), Tagalog araw (“sun”), Māori ao (“daytime”)).

words.g: breast
words.e: Cognate with Northern Thai ᨶᩫ᩠ᨾ, Lao ນົມ (nom), Lü ᦓᦳᧄ (num), Shan ၼူမ်း (núum), Tai Dam ꪶꪙꪣ, Ahom 𑜃𑜤𑜪 (nuṃ), Zhuang noemz.

words.g: dry curry (thickened spicy Thai curry with large pieces of roast chicken, pork or beef).
words.e: Unknown, some have linked it to be a loan word from Malay panggang (“to grill; grilled”), although this is doubtful, judging by the consonants. First attested in 1890 as a type of "grilled chicken" (see also at the Wikipedia article).

words.g: to return; to come back.
words.e: Compare Lao ກັບ (kap).

words.g: stone; rock
words.e: From Proto-Tai *triːlᴬ (“stone”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩉᩥ᩠ᨶ, Lao ຫີນ (hīn), Lü ᦠᦲᧃ (ḣiin), Tai Dam ꪬꪲꪙ, Shan ႁိၼ် (hǐn), Tai Nüa ᥞᥤᥢᥴ (hín), Ahom 𑜍𑜢𑜃𑜫 (rin), Nong Zhuang tin, Zhuang rin, Saek หรี่น.

words.g: round or roundish figure: circle, ring, egg, etc.
words.e: From Old Khmer វាង៑ (vāṅ), វាង្ង៑ (vāṅṅ), វង៑ (vaṅ, “enclosure; citadel, fort, fortress, stronghold; palace; to encircle, to enclose, to surround; to bar, to block; to screen, to shield; etc”), from Proto-Mon-Khmer *wa(a)ŋ (“enclosure”). Cognate with Khmer វង់ (vŭəng), Lao ວົງ (wong). Doublet of วั…

words.g: pencil made of white soil or rock, as marl or limestone, used for writing on a slate
words.e: Compound of ดิน (din, “soil”) + สอ (sɔ̌ɔ, “white”).

words.g: yellow
words.e: From Proto-Tai *ʰlɯəŋᴬ (“yellow”). Cognate with Lao ເຫຼືອງ (lư̄ang), Lü ᦵᦜᦲᧂ (l̇oeng), Shan လိူင် (lǒeng), Ahom 𑜎𑜢𑜤𑜂𑜫 (lüṅ), Zhuang lieng.

words.g: old (having existed for a long time).
words.e: From Proto-Tai *kawᴮ (“old (of non-living things)”), from Middle Chinese 故 (MC kuH, “old”). Cognate with Lao ເກົ່າ (kao), Tai Nüa ᥐᥝᥱ (kǎw), Lü ᦂᧁᧈ (k̇aw¹), Tai Dam ꪹꪀ꪿ꪱ, Shan ၵဝ်ႇ (kào), Ahom 𑜀𑜧 (kaw), Zhuang gaeuq.

words.g: expensive; of a high price.
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *bɛːŋᴬ² (“expensive”), from Proto-Tai *beːŋᴬ (“expensive”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨻᩯ᩠ᨦ, Lao ແພງ (phǣng), Lü ᦶᦗᧂ (paeng), Shan ပႅင်း (péng), Zhuang bengz, Nong Zhuang biangz or byangz. Compare Sui mbingl (“expensive”).

words.s: ฝนตกไม่ทั่วฟ้า
words.g: to distribute or give away something in a discriminate or biased manner.
words.e: From ฝน (fǒn, “rain”) + ตก (dtòk, “to fall”) + ไม่ (mâi, “not”) + ทั่ว (tûua, “all over”) + ฟ้า (fáa, “heaven; sky”); literally "rain falls not from all over the sky".

words.s: หนีเสือปะจระเข้
words.g: to escape from one bad situation only to meet another bad situation.
words.e: From หนี (nǐi, “to escape; to flee”) + เสือ (sʉ̌ʉa, “tiger”) + ปะ (bpà, “to meet”) + จระเข้ (jɔɔ-rá-kêe, “crocodile”), literally "to escape from a tiger only to meet a crocodile".

words.s: ตีเหล็กเมื่อแดง กินแกงเมื่อร้อน
words.g: strike while the iron is hot.
words.e: Literally: Strike the iron when it's red, and eat the curry when it's hot.

words.s: สามีเป็นช้างเท้าหน้า ภรรยาเป็นช้างเท้าหลัง
words.g: it's a sad house where the hen crows louder than the cock.
words.e: Literally: Husband is elephant's front legs, wife is elephant's hind legs. (Husbands always lead, and wives always follow.)

words.g: age: length of life
words.e: From Pali อายุ (āyu, “age”), from Sanskrit อายุ (āyu); probably via Old Khmer ʼāyuḥ, ʼāyu° (“age; life; lifespan”). Compare Modern Khmer អាយុ (aayʊ’); Lao ອາຍຸ (ʼ).

words.g: white elephant, traditionally believed to be one of the seven precious things, known as ส…
words.e: From ช้าง (cháang, “elephant”) + เผือก (pʉ̀ʉak, “white”).

words.g: person specialising in something: expert, specialist, professional, etc.
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *ʰmɔːᴬ (“shaman”), from Proto-Tai *ʰmoːᴬ (“shaman”), from Old Chinese 巫 (OC *ma). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩉ᩠ᨾᩬᩴ, Khün ᩉ᩠ᨾᩳ, Lao ໝໍ (mǭ), Lü ᦖᦸ (ṁoa), Tai Dam ꪢꪷ, Shan မေႃ (mǎu), Tai Nüa ᥛᥨᥝᥴ (mów), Ahom 𑜉𑜦𑜡 (mō), 𑜈𑜦𑜡 (bō), or 𑜈𑜨𑜦𑜡 (bwō), Zhuang mo (as in bohmo), Nong…

words.g: one who ignites.
words.e: From Pali ḍāhaka (“fire; one who burns”).

words.g: body hair
words.e: Borrowed from Pali vāla (“hair of the tail”) and Sanskrit वाल (vāla, “of the tail hair”), which can yield both initial ว and initial พ, and also from the synonymous by-forms Pali bāla and Sanskrit बाल (bāla).

words.g: arm (upper limb of the body).
words.e: Borrowed from Pali bāhu (“arm”), from Sanskrit बाहु (bāhu, “arm”).

words.g: a first person pronoun used when addressing a person of equal or higher status: I, we, et…
words.e: Possibly from contraction of ข้า (kâa, “slave; servant”) + พระเจ้า (prá-jâao, literally “sacred lord”), literally meaning "sacred lord's servant" or "sacred lord's slave". Compare Lao ຂ້າພະເຈົ້າ (khā pha chao).

words.g: a second person pronoun: you.
words.e:
From Proto-Tai *mɯŋᴬ (“singular second-person pronoun (weak)”).
Cognate with Lao ມຶງ (mưng), Lü ᦙᦹᧂ (mueng), Tai Dam ꪣꪳꪉ, Zhuang mwngz.
Compare Proto-Hlai *C-mɯː (“you (singular)”).

words.g: hawksbill sea turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata)
words.e: Borrowed from Old Khmer kras. Traditionally grouped with the "freckle" sense of Etymology 2, due to hawksbill sea turtles having spotted patterns, though whether the two are related is uncertain.

words.g: big sack.

words.s: กระดูกเชิงกราน
words.g: pelvic bone
words.e: From กระดูก (grà-dùuk, “bone”) + เชิงกราน (chəəng-graan, “pelvis”).

words.g: one who practises or is expert in law: jurist, lawyer, etc.
words.e: From นัก (nák, agent noun prefix) + กฎหมาย (gòt-mǎai, “law”).

words.g: water diver.
words.e: นัก (nák, “agent noun prefix”) + ดำน้ำ (dam-náam, “to dive into water; to ad lib, to improvise, to extemporise”).

words.g: person imprisoned for a crime: prisoner, inmate, etc.
words.e: From นัก (nák, agent noun prefix) + โทษ (tôot, “punishment; penalty”).

words.g: person fond of something; person specialising in something.
words.e: From นัก (nák, agentive prefix) + เลง (leeng, from Khmer លេង (leeng, “to play”)).

words.g: Shan people or person.
words.e: ไท (tai, “Tai”) + ใหญ่ (yài, “big”); possibly calque of Shan တႆးလူင် (tái lǔung, “Shan”, literally “Big Tai”).

words.g: Shan people or person.
words.e: From Burmese ရှမ်း (hram:), from Thai สยาม (sà-yǎam). Doublet of สยาม (sà-yǎam).

words.g: a second person pronoun used to address a person of equal or lower status or used to addr…
words.e: Probably from Old Khmer ឯង (eṅa), ឯង៑ (eṅ, “self; oneself; own; personally”). Cognate with Modern Khmer ឯង (ʼaeng, “you; self, oneself; etc”). Doublet of เอง (eeng). Compare Proto-Vietic *ʔɛːŋ; Vietnamese anh (“you”).

words.g: sweet potato
words.e: From มัน (man, “tuber”) + เทศ (têet, “foreign”).

words.g: pirate: sea robber.
words.e: Semi-learned borrowing from Malay selat (“strait: narrow water channel”).

words.g: louse (Pediculus humanus), especially head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis).
words.e: From Proto-Tai *trawᴬ (“head louse”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᩉᩮᩢᩣ, Lao ເຫົາ (hao), Lü ᦠᧁ (ḣaw), Tai Dam ꪹꪬꪱ, Shan ႁဝ် (hǎo), Saek เหร่า, Zhuang raeu.

words.g: sand (the more or less fine debris of rocks)
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *zaːjᴬ⁴ (“sand”), from Proto-Tai *zwɯəjᴬ (“sand”), from Old Chinese 沙 (OC *sraːl, *sraːls, “sand”). Cognate with Northern Thai ᨪᩣ᩠ᨿ, Lao ຊາຍ (sāi), Lü ᦌᦻ (saay), Khün ᨪᩣ᩠ᨿ, Shan သၢႆး (sáai), Tai Nüa ᥔᥣᥭᥰ (säay), Ahom 𑜏𑜩 (say) or 𑜏𑜩𑜤 (sayu), Zhuang saiz, Nong Zhuang saiz.…

words.g: to give a signal.
words.e: ให้ (hâi, “to give, to allow”) + สัญญา (sǎn-yaa)

words.g: water chestnut or water caltrop (Trapa bicornis).
Thai pi (any of a variety of quadruple-reed Thai oboes); wind instrument.
words.e: From Proto-Southwestern Tai *piːᴮ¹ (“flute”). Cognate with Lao ປີ່ (pī), Northern Thai ᨸᩦ᩵, Khün ᨸᩦ᩵, Lü ᦔᦲᧈ (ṗii¹), Shan ပီႇ (pìi), Tai Dam ꪜꪲ꪿, Tai Nüa ᥙᥤᥱ (pǐ), Phake ပ︀ီ (pī), Ahom 𑜆𑜣 (pī).

words.g: tree jasmine: Millingtonia hortensis.
Ravana, the demon king with ten necks
words.e: From ทศ (tót, “ten”) + กัณฐ์ (“throat; neck”); literally "ten necks" or "ten-necked"; ultimately made from Sanskrit दश (daśa, “ten”) and कण्ठ (kaṇṭha, “neck”). Compare with Telugu దశకంఠుడు (daśakaṇṭhuḍu) and Burmese ဒဿဂီရိ (da.ssa.giri.).

words.g: a kind of timber tree
weapon; arm
words.e: Borrowed from Pali āvudha (“weapon”). Compare Lao ອາວຸດ (ʼā wut), Modern Khmer អាវុធ (ʼaavut).

words.g: good reputation; good fame; good name; honour
words.e: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit कीर्ति (kīrti, “reputation”). Doublet of กีรติ. Compare Pali kitti, whence Thai กิตติ (gìt-dtì).

words.g: The first letter of the Indonesian alphabet, written in the Latin script.
words.e: From the Latin letter A, from the Etruscan letter 𐌀 (a), from the Ancient Greek letter Α (A, “alpha”), derived from the Phoenician letter 𐤀 (ʾ, “aleph”), from the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓃾.

words.g: an exchange of two comparable things.
words.e: Borrowed from English swap.

words.g: The sixth letter of the Indonesian alphabet, written in the Latin script.
a powdered larvacide, see temefos for further information
words.e: A genericized trademark of a BASF trademark.

words.g: The twenty-fifth letter of the Indonesian alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The name of the Latin script letter D/d.
words.e: From Dutch dee.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter N/n.
words.e: From Dutch en.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter T/t.
words.e: From Dutch tee.

words.g: The fifteenth letter of the Indonesian alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The ninth letter of the Indonesian alphabet, written in the Latin script.
The name of the Latin script letter B/b.
words.e: From Dutch bee.

words.g: boot: a heavy shoe that covers part of the leg
words.e: Borrowed from English boot, from Middle English boote, bote (“shoe”), from Old French bote (“a high, thick shoe”). Compare Standard Malay but.

words.g: an institution where one can place and borrow money and take care of financial affairs
words.e: Unadapted borrowing from Dutch bank (“bank”). Doublet of banco and bangku.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter L/l.
words.e: From Dutch el.

words.g: a flightless bird of the order Apterygiformes native to New Zealand.
words.e: Borrowed from Māori kiwi.

words.g: water (clear liquid H₂O)
words.e: Inherited from Malay air, from Proto-Malayic *air, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *wahiʀ.

words.g: harvested young garlic at the age of 70 days after planting
human, person
words.e: From Malay orang, from Old Malay urang, from Proto-Malayic *uraŋ (“person”), from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *uʀaŋ (“outsider”). Doublet of bong and wong.

words.g: the spirit of a deceased person is believed to visit his relatives as a notification that…
words.e: Borrowed from Bulungan [Term?].

words.g: relating to the mouth
words.e: Ultimately derived from Late Latin ōrālis, perhaps through Dutch oraal.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter W/w.
words.e: From Dutch wee.

words.g: silver (metal)
words.e: Inherited from Malay perak, from earlier pirak. See there for further etymology.

words.g: first person singular pronoun: I, me, my
words.e: From Malay saya, from earlier sahaya, from Sanskrit सहाय (sahāya).

words.g: book (collection of sheets of paper bound together containing printed or written material)
words.e: From Malay buku, from Dutch boek, from Middle Dutch boec, from Old Dutch buoc, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. The addition of the last syllable might be due to the similar existing word, see Etymology 2 below.

words.g: cat (domestic species)
words.e: Inherited from Malay kucing, from Classical Malay kucing, from (Western) Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kutiŋ. Compare Tagalog kuting.

words.g: first person singular pronoun: I, me, my
words.e: Inherited from Malay aku, from Proto-Malayic *aku, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *aku, from Proto-Austronesian *aku. False cognate of Latin ego and Ancient Greek ἐγώ (egṓ).

words.g: house (abode)
words.e: Inherited from Malay rumah, from Classical Malay رومه (“house”), from Proto-Malayic *rumah, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ʀumaq, from Proto-Austronesian *ʀumaq.

words.g: friend
words.e: From Malay teman, from Classical Malay [script needed] (teman), from Tamil தமன் (tamaṉ, “friend; relative”). Mostly displaced native kawan, now usage mostly restricted in animals, while Standard Malay still uses it more often than teman.

words.g: time (instance or occurrence)
words.e: From Malay kali, from Sanskrit काल (kāla, “time”). Doublet of kala.

words.g: moon (largest natural satellite of planet Earth)
words.e: Inherited from Malay bulan, from Proto-Malayic *bulan, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *bulan, from Proto-Austronesian *bulaN. Doublet of rembulan and wulan. The sense “any natural satellite of a planet” is a semantic loan from Dutch maan (“moon”).

words.g: river (a large and often winding stream which drains a land mass)
words.e: Inherited from Malay sungai, from Proto-Malayic *suŋay.

words.g: first person plural inclusive (including you) pronoun: we, us, our
words.e: Inherited from Malay kita, from Proto-Malayic *kita(ʔ), from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *(i-)kita, from Proto-Austronesian *(i-)kita.

words.g: first person plural exclusive (not including you) pronoun: we, us, our
words.e: Inherited from Malay kami, from Proto-Malayic *kami, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kami, from Proto-Austronesian *kami.

words.g: mother (female parent)
words.e: Originally from baby talk.

words.g: a needle without an eye (usually) made of drawn-out steel wire with one end sharpened and…
words.e: From Dutch pin, from Proto-Germanic *pinnaz *pinnaz, *pinnō, *pint- (“protruding point, peak, peg, pin, nail”), from Proto-Indo-European *bend- 'protruding object, pointed peg, nail, edge'.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter R/r.
words.e: From Dutch er.

words.g: go (a kind of strategic board game)
words.e: Borrowed from Japanese 碁(ご) (go).

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter Y/y.
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch jee. Doublet of je.

words.g: stone chipping
words.e: Unadapted borrowing from Dutch split.

words.g: law (rule)
words.e: From Dutch wet.

words.g: flat house

word (the smallest discrete, meaningful unit of language)
words.e: From Malay kata, from Pali kathā, from Sanskrit कथा (kathā, “speech; story”).

words.g: blood (vital liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
words.e: From Malay darah, from Proto-Malayic *darah, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *daʀaq, from Proto-Austronesian *daʀaq.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter M/m.
words.e: From Dutch em.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter G/g.
words.e: From Dutch gee.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter C/c.
cold beverage
words.e: From Malay es from Dutch ijs, from Middle Dutch ijs, from Old Dutch *īs, from Proto-Germanic *īsą, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eyH-.

words.g: father
words.e: Borrowed from Betawi baba.

words.g: aviator, pilot: A person who is in charge of the controls of an aircraft
words.e: Internationalism, borrowed from English pilot, from Middle French pilot, pillot, from Italian pilota, piloto, older also pedotta, pedot(t)o (the form in pil- is probably influenced by pileggiare (“to sail, navigate”)); ultimately from unattested Byzantine Greek *πηδώτης (*pēdṓtēs, “helmsman”), from…

words.g: lava: the molten rock ejected by a volcano (hence on the surface) from its crater or fiss…
words.e: Internationalism, borrowed from Dutch lava, from Italian lava, from Neapolitan and Sicilian lava (“lava; downpour overflowing the streets”), likely from Latin lābēs (“a fall; a collapse; subsidence”).

words.g: indicates an approximate number
words.e: Unadapted borrowing from Dutch à, from French à, from Old French a, a merge of Latin ad and ab.

words.g: bottled water
words.e: A genericized trademark of the Indonesian trademark Aqua, from Latin aqua (“water”).

words.g: bagel: a toroidal bread roll that is boiled before it is baked
words.e: From English bagel, from Yiddish בייגל (beygl), ultimately from a diminutive of Middle High German bouc, boug- (“ring, bracelet”), from Old High German boug (“ring”), from Proto-Germanic *baugaz (“ring”).

words.g: fan: a person who is fond of something or someone
words.e: From English fan (“a person who is fond of something or someone”), clipping of fanatic.

words.g: a small room or compartment
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch cel (“cell”), from Middle Dutch celle, from Latin cella.

words.g: a short film clip, with or without audio (as in a music video, or one of the plethora of…
words.e: From English video, from the root vide of Latin videō (“to see”) + -o.

words.g: to play
words.e: Inherited from Malay main, from Proto-Malayic *main, a reduction from Pre-Proto-Malayic *qumaim, *qumayam, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *-um- + *qayam (“domesticated animal, plaything”). The "unpromptedly" sense is a semantic loan from Betawi maèn or an Eastern Indonesian Malay form (compare Kupang…

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter J/j.
words.e: From Dutch jee. Doublet of ye. Represented Dutch-derived J (pronounced /j/, modern Y) before 1972.

words.g: novel: a work of prose fiction, longer than a novella
words.e: Inherited from Malay roman, from Dutch roman.

words.g: bitter gourd
words.e: From Javanese ꦥꦫꦺ (paré). Doublet of paria and peria.

words.g: fish (vertebrate animal)
words.e: Inherited from Malay ikan, from Proto-Malayic *ikan, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *hikan, from Proto-Austronesian *Sikan. The last component -kan is related to makan (“to eat”).

words.g: rouge: Red or pink makeup to add colour to the cheeks; blusher
words.e: Unadapted borrowing from French rouge (“red”), from Middle French rouge, from Old French roge, rouge, from Latin rubeus.

words.g: a group of three people or things.
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch trio, from Italian trio.

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter Z/z.
words.e: From Dutch zet.

words.g: The fifteenth book of the Old Testament and a book of the Hebrew Tanakh
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch Ezra, from Biblical Hebrew עֶזְרָא.

words.g: tripod: a three-legged stand or mount
words.e: Borrowed from English tripod.

words.g: agape: love; the love between man and God; Christian love feasts
words.e: From Ancient Greek ἀγάπη (agápē, “love; the love between man and God; Christian love feasts”).

words.g: a male given name from Javanese
words.e: From Javanese Adi, from Sanskrit अधि (adhi).

words.g: father
words.e: Inherited from Malay bapa. Doublet of bapak. See there for further etymology.

words.g: time (inevitable passing of events)
words.e: From Malay waktu, from Arabic وَقْت (waqt, “time”). Displaced native lamaan (“period, time”), luangan (“free time”), and non-native kala (“period, eld”), masa (“time, period, era”).

words.g: close friend, best friend
words.e: From Malay sahabat, from Classical Malay صحابة (sahabat), from Arabic صَحَابَة (ṣaḥāba). Doublet of sobat.

words.g: wood (substance)
words.e: From Malay kayu, from Proto-Malayic *kayuʔ, from Proto-Malayo-Chamic, from Proto-Malayo-Sumbawan, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kahiw, from Proto-Austronesian *kaSiw.

words.g: having a small distance between ends or edges
words.e: Inherited from Malay pendek

words.g: third person plural pronoun: they, them, their
words.e: From Malay mereka, from earlier mareka, from Old Javanese marika. Displaced Proto-Malayic *sida(ʔ) (whence Iban sida).

words.g: black (absorbing all light)
words.e: From Malay hitam, from Proto-Malayic *hitəm, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *(ma-)qitəm.

words.g: love (in general senses)
words.e:
Inherited from Malay cinta, from Sanskrit चिन्ता (cintā, “thinking, sad, care, anxiety, consideration”).
* Moslty displaced native sayang.

words.g: to eat (to consume, ingest)
words.e: Inherited from Malay makan, from Proto-Malayic *makan, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kaən, from Proto-Austronesian *kaən. Doublet of pakan and pangan.

words.g: foot (short foot-like projection on the bottom of an object to support it)
words.e: Inherited from Malay kaki, from Proto-Malayic *kaki, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *qaqay, from Proto-Austronesian *qaqay.

words.g: small stove
words.e: Borrowed from Hokkien 洪爐 /洪炉 (âng-lô͘, “large oven; great furnace”), from Hokkien 洪 (âng, “vast, immense”) + 爐 /炉 (lô͘, “fireplace, stove, oven, furnace”).

words.g: father
words.e: Infixation of bapak + -ok-.

words.g: to eat
to hear
words.e: Inherited from Malay dengar, from Proto-Malayic *dəŋər, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *dəŋəʀ. Doublet of rungu (“hearing ability”).

words.g: father
words.e: From Malay bapa, bapak, from Old Javanese bapa, ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *appa. Doublet of bapa. Hoogervorst mentioned that the word was affixed as *ba- (“someone who fulfils the function of or behaves like”) + apak, which is cognate of Tamil அப்பா (appā, “father”), and comparable to modern…

words.g: rich guy, rich people
words.e: Blend of orang (“human”) + kaya (“rich”).

words.g: ten thousand
words.e: From Betawi ceban (“ten thousand”), from Hokkien 一萬 /一万 (chi̍t-bān, “ten thousand”).

words.g: sand (finely ground rock)
words.e: Inherited from Malay pasir, from Proto-Malayic *pasir, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *pasiʀ (“sandbank, shoal in river or sea”). Doublet of Paser.

words.g: a young creature
words.e: Inherited from Malay anak, from Classical Malay انق (anak), from Proto-Malayic *anak, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *anak, from Proto-Austronesian *aNak.

words.g: to kill
words.e: Inherited from Malay bunuh, from Proto-Malayic *bunuh, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *bunuq, from Proto-Austronesian *buNuq.

words.g: second person pronoun: you, your
words.e: From Malay kamu, from Proto-Malayic *kamu(ʔ) (“you, your (plural)”), from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *(i-)kamu, *kamiu, from Proto-Austronesian *(i-)kamu, *kamiu.

words.g: to kill
words.e: From Malay membunuh. Equivalent to meng- + bunuh.

words.g: to run amok
words.e: Inherited from Malay اموق (amuk), from Javanese ꦲꦩꦸꦏ꧀ (amuk), from Old Javanese amūk, from aN- + wūk (“furious attack”), probably onomatopoeic.

words.g: come on!
words.e: From Malay ayuh, ayo, from Classical Malay ايوه (ayuh), ايو (ayo). Cognate of Malay ayuh and Javanese ꦲꦪꦺꦴ (ayo, “come on, let's, please”).

words.g: to read (to look at and interpret letters or other information)
words.e: From Malay baca, from Sanskrit वाचा (vācā, “speech, word”).

words.g: iron (element)
words.e: From Malay besi, from Proto-Malayic *bəsi, from Proto-Malayo-Chamic *bəsi.

words.g: when: during the time that
words.e:
From Malay kala, from Classical Malay kala, from Sanskrit काल (kāla, “time”) or Sanskrit कला (kalā, “a division of time”). Doublet of kali.
Semantic loan from Dutch tijd (“tense”, literally “time”).

words.g: to go out, to get out, to exit
words.e: Inherited from Malay keluar. By surface analysis, ke- + luar.

words.g: novel: a work of prose fiction, longer than a novella
words.e: From Dutch novelle, from Italian novella, from Latin novella, feminine of novellus. Doublet of novela and novelet.

words.g: cloud (a visible mass of water droplets suspended in the air)
words.e: Inherited from Malay awan, from Proto-Malayic *awan, Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *hawan.

words.g: alb: a long, white robe worn by priests and other ministers, underneath most of the other…
words.e: Learned borrowing from Latin alba (as in tunica alba (“white tunic”), vestis alba (“white garment”)), feminine of albus (“white”).

words.g: albino: person or animal congenitally lacking melanin pigmentation in the skin, eyes, and…
words.e: From Dutch albino, from Spanish albino, from Latin albus.

words.g: New Guinea (a large island in the Pacific Ocean)
white cambric
words.e:
* From Dutch moiré, from French moiré, from Arabic مُخَيَّر (muḵayyar, literally “chosen”).
* From Tamil முறி (muṟi).

words.g: name (word or phrase indicating a particular person, place, class or thing)
words.e: From Malay nama (“name”), from Classical Malay nama (“name”), from Sanskrit नामन् (nā́man), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnā́ma, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥ (“name”). Cognate with English name and Dutch naam, but not Japanese 名前 (なまえ, namae, “name”), 名 (な, na), お名前 (おなまえ, o-namae, “name”). Double…

words.g: bravo, well done!, good show!
words.e: Borrowed from Italian bravo.

words.g: a female given name from Latin, equivalent to English Claudia
words.e: From Latin Claudia.

words.g: a male given name from Arabic used by Muslims
words.e: From Arabic عَبْد (ʕabd, “servant [of]”) + ال (al-, “the”).

words.g: in the year
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch anno, from Latin annō, ablative of annus.

words.g: silver
words.e: Learned borrowing from Latin argentum (“silver”).

words.g: aviator, pilot: A person who is in charge of the controls of an aircraft
words.e: Internationalism.

words.g: love, especially sexual love or sensuality
words.e: From Sanskrit काम (kāma, “love”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *káHmas (“desire”), from Proto-Indo-European *kóh₂-mo-s, from *keh₂- (“to desire, wish”).

words.g: a male given name from Ancient Greek, equivalent to English Andrew
words.e: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek Ἀνδρέᾱς (Andréās).

words.g: milestone, one of a series of numbered markers placed along a road at regular intervals,…
words.e: From Dutch paal (“pole”), from Middle Dutch pâel, from Old Dutch pāl, from Latin pālus. Semantic loan from Dutch mijlpaal (“milestone”).

words.g: flower bud
words.e: Learned borrowing from Old Javanese kuḍu (“bud”).

words.g: god (male deity)
words.e: From Malay dewa, from Sanskrit देव (deva, “god”).

words.g: ninja, a person trained in ninjutsu, especially one used for espionage, assassination, an…
words.e: Borrowed from Japanese 忍者(にんじゃ) (ninja).

words.g: king soldierbream, Bowen snapper, long-spined red bream, longfin snapper, longspine seabr…
words.e: Unknown

words.g: wind (movement of air)
words.e: Inherited from Malay pawana, from Sanskrit पवन (pavana).

words.g: black pepper (Piper nigrum)
words.e:
Inherited from Malay lada, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lajaq or *laja.
* Semantic loan from Minangkabau lado (“chili pepper”) whether through first contact in progenitor Malay dialects or later post-independence.

words.g: teacher: a person who teaches, especially one employed in a school
words.e: From Malay guru, via Old Javanese, ultimately Sanskrit गुरु (gurú, “guru, teacher, sage”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *gr̥Húṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gr̥Húš, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥h₂ús (“heavy”). Doublet of brutal and bruto.

words.g: husband
words.e: From Malay laki, from Classical Malay [Term?], from Old Malay lāki, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *laki, from Proto-Austronesian *laki.

words.g: superior: a person of higher rank or quality, especially a colleague in a higher position.
words.e: Internationalism, from Latin superior.

words.g: giant taro, elephant ear taro (Alocasia macrorrhizos)
white mite in rice husks
words.e: From Riau Malay [Term?].

words.g: gold (element)
words.e: Inherited from Malay emas. See there for further etymology.

words.g: a female given name from Javanese
words.e: From Javanese Arum.

words.g: boa, snake of the genus Boa
words.e: From Dutch boa, from Middle Dutch boa, from Latin boa.

words.g: canine tooth
words.e: Inherited from Malay taring, from Classical Malay taring.

words.g: house (abode)
words.e: Inherited from Malay bait, from Arabic بَيْت (bayt), from Proto-Semitic *bayt-.

words.g: bonanza, gold mine, lucky strike, sweet deal
words.e: Borrowed from Spanish bonanza (“calm sea, fair weather, good luck, rich lode”), from Medieval Latin bonacia (“fair weather”), a blend of bonus (“good”) + malacia (“calm sea”).

words.g: fatal; causing death or destruction
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch fataal, from Middle French fatal, from Latin fātālis.

words.g: alleyway, alley, narrow street. A narrow pathway bound by walls on both sides
words.e: From Dutch gang (“passageway, alley”), from Middle Dutch ganc, from Old Dutch gank, gang, from Proto-Germanic *gangaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰongʰ-o-s, from *ǵʰengʰ- (“to step; stride”). Doublet of geng.

words.g: a separate portion; a number of things taken collectively
words.e: From Dutch lot, from Proto-Germanic *hlutą.

words.g: small Indian civet (Viverricula indica)
words.e: From Javanese ꦫꦱꦺ (rasé).

words.g: stadium: a life stage of an organism
words.e: From Dutch stadium (“stadium, life stage; stage, phase”), from Latin stadium (“a measure of length, a race course”), from Ancient Greek στάδιον (stádion, “a measure of length, a running track”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-. Doublet of stadion.

words.g: ten thousand
words.e: From Malay laksa, from Classical Malay لقسا (laksa), from Sanskrit लक्ष (lakṣa, “hundred thousand”).

words.g: stone, rock
words.e:
Inherited from Malay batu, from Proto-Malayic *batu, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *batu, from Proto-Austronesian *batux.
* For the sense of battery, compare Betawi batu (“stone, battery cell”), dialectal Chinese 電石／电石 (“battery”, literally “electric stone”), and Japanese 電石(エレクトレット) (erekutoretto,…

words.g: small amount of money left for a waiter, taxi driver, etc. as a token of appreciation
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch tip, from English tip.

words.g: the twenty-second letter of the Arabic alphabet. ك (k)
words.e: From Arabic ك (k, “kaf”).

words.g: a female given name from French
words.e: Pronunciations with final schwa are reinforced by Dutch Anne. Ultimately from French Anne.

words.g: mestizo: a person of mixed ancestry, especially one of Spanish and Native American herita…
words.e: Borrowed from Spanish mestizo (“mestizo”), from Latin mixtus (“mixed”).

words.g: a dry measure (for dates, water, grains, and other things) varying in size, roughly aroun…
words.e: Ultimately from Arabic مُدّ (mudd, “a certain dry measure”)

words.g: The name of the Latin script letter Q/q.
words.e: From Dutch quu.

words.g: a male given name from Latin [in turn from Ancient Greek, in turn from Hebrew].
words.e: Learned borrowing from Latin Gabriel, from Ancient Greek Γαβρῑήλ (Gabrīḗl), from Biblical Hebrew גַּבְרִיאֵל (Gaḇrīʾḗl, “God is my strong man”), גֶּבֶר (géver, “strong man, hero”) and אֵל (ʾēl, “God”).

words.g: to sleep
words.e: Possibly a clipping of nina bobo (“lullaby”)

words.g: guard, person who or thing that protects something
words.e: From Portuguese guarda, guardar, from Old Galician-Portuguese guardar, from Medieval Latin wardō, from Frankish *wardōn, from Proto-Germanic *wardāną (“to guard”), from Proto-Indo-European *wer- (“to heed, defend”). Doublet of gardu.

words.g: bad breath, halitosis
words.e: Borrowed from Javanese ꦲꦧꦧ꧀ (abab), from Old Javanese abab (“breathing, exhaling”), from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *epap (“clap, flap, slap”).

words.g: A drum, usually one belonging to a drum kit
words.e: Borrowed from Dutch drum, from English drum.

words.g: one of the names of the first vowel in the Tamil abugida, அ (a)
words.e: Compound of அ (a) + கரம் (karam).

words.g: lakh, one hundred thousand (100,000 or 1,00,000)
words.e: From Sanskrit लक्ष (lakṣa).

words.g: to chew; eat by biting or nibbling
words.e: Cognate with Telugu కరచు (karacu). Compare கொறி (koṟi).

words.g: a Hindu; a person adhering to Hinduism
words.e: Borrowed from Hindi हिंदू (hindū), from Classical Persian هندو (hindū), ultimately either directly derived from Sanskrit सिन्धु (sindhu) or through Proto-Iranian *sindʰu.

words.g: a title of a king of the Pandya dynasty
words.e: From செழி (ceḻi, “to prosper, multiply”) + -அன் (-aṉ, masculine suffix particle).

words.g: Indian Ocean
person
words.e: From Old Tamil 𑀆𑀴𑁆 (āḷ), from Proto-Dravidian *āḷ. Cognate with Kannada ಆಳು (āḷu), Malayalam ആള് (āḷŭ), Telugu ఆలు (ālu).

words.g: betel leaf
words.e:
Inherited from Old Tamil 𑀇𑀮𑁃 (ilai), from Proto-South Dravidian *elay.
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಎಲೆ (ele), Old Kannada ಎಲೆ (ele), Tulu ಇರೆ (ire)/Tulu ಇಲೆ (ile), Malayalam ഇല (ila), Kodava [script needed] (elakaṇḍa), Toda [script needed] (es̱), Kota (India) [script needed] (el).

words.g: to lull; to rock a child in a cradle with lullabies
words.e: From தால் (tāl, “tongue”) + ஆட்டு (āṭṭu, “to move, dance”).

words.g: world, earth
words.e: Inherited from Old Tamil 𑀉𑀮𑀓𑀫𑁆 (ulakam), from Sanskrit लोक (loka). Doublet of லோகம் (lōkam).

words.g: five (numeral:௫)
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *caymtu (“five”). Cognate with Kannada ಐದು (aidu), Malayalam അഞ്ച് (añcŭ), Telugu ఐదు (aidu), Tulu ಅಯಿನ್ (ayinŭ).

words.g: one (numeral: ௧)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *o-?
Proto-Dravidian *on
Proto-Dravidian *-ṯu
Proto-Dravidian *onṯu
Tamil ஒன்று
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *on-ṯu (“one”).
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಒಂದು (ondu), Malayalam ഒന്ന് (onnŭ), Telugu ఒండు (oṇḍu), Tulu ಒಂಜಿ (oñji). False cognate of English one.

words.g: tongue
words.e: Probably from நால் (nāl).

words.g: tongue
words.e: From நக்கு (nakku, “to lick”). Cognate with Malayalam നാക്ക് (nākkŭ).

words.g: old man or aged man
words.e: From கிழவு (kiḻavu, “old age”) + -அன் (-aṉ), from the root கிழ (kiḻa, “old”). See Tamil கிழமை (kiḻamai) for more cognates. Compare with Malayalam കിഴവൻ (kiḻavaṉ).

words.g: to stand
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *nil-
Tamil நில்
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *nil- (“to stand, wait, stop”). Cognate with Kannada ನಿಲ್ಲು (nillu), Malayalam നിൽക്കുക (nilkkuka), Telugu నిలుచు (nilucu).

words.g: a female given name from Tamil
words.e:
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *nelanc(c)- (“moonlight, moon”).
Cognate with Malayalam നിലാവ് (nilāvŭ), Telugu నెల (nela), Kodava ನೆಲಚಿ (nelaci), Kolami नेल (nela).

words.g: horse (a hoofed mammal, Equus ferus caballus, often used throughout history for riding an…
words.e:
From Proto-Dravidian *kut-ir-ay (from Proto-Dravidian *kut-i (“to jump”), whence குதி (kuti)).
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಕುದುರೆ (kudure), Malayalam കുതിര (kutira), Telugu గుర్రము (gurramu), Tulu ಕುದುರೆ (kudure). Compare Sanskrit घोटक (ghoṭaka), a Dravidian borrowing.

words.g: to bark, as a dog
words.e: Compare குரை (kurai).

words.g: two (numeral: ௨)
words.e:
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *ir-aṇ-ṭu (“two”).
Cognates
Cognate with Kannada ಎರಡು (eraḍu), Kolami ऎरण्डि (eraṇḍi), Malayalam രണ്ട് (raṇṭŭ), Telugu రెండు (reṇḍu), Tulu ಎರಡ್ (eraḍŭ).

words.g: the five kinds of metals
words.e: Compound of ஐம் (aim, combining form of ஐ (ai, “five”)) + பொன் (poṉ, “metal, gold”). Cognate with Malayalam ഐമ്പൊന്ന് (aimponnŭ).

words.g: unripe mango fruit
words.e:
Inherited from Proto-South Dravidian *mām-kāy (“(unripe) mango”). By surface analysis, மாம் (mām, “mango”) + காய் (kāy, “unripe fruit”).
Cognate with Kannada ಮಾವಿನಕಾಯಿ (māvinakāyi), Malayalam മാങ്ങ (māṅṅa), Telugu మామిడికాయ (māmiḍikāya).

words.g: letter (written message)
words.e: Borrowed from Portuguese cartaz. Compare Malayalam കടലാസ് (kaṭalāsŭ).

words.g: creek, rivulet, small river
words.e: From ஓடு (ōṭu, “to run, flow, operate”). Cognate with Malayalam ഓട (ōṭa). Compare Marathi ओढा (oḍhā).

words.g: form three gerund of ஆடு (āṭu, “to shake, dance, play, bathe”).
words.e:
Etymology tree
Tamil ஆடு (āṭu)
Tamil -அல் (-al)
Tamil ஆடல்
From ஆடு (āṭu) + -அல் (-al).

words.g: three (numeral:௩)
words.e:
Inherited from Old Tamil 𑀫𑀽𑀷𑁰𑀶𑀼 (mūṉṟu), from Proto-Dravidian *muHnṯu (“three”).
Cognates
Cognate with Old Kannada ಮೂಡ್ರು (mūḍru), Kannada ಮೂರು (mūru), Malayalam മൂന്നു (mūnnu), Old Telugu మూన్ౚు (mūnṟ̄u), Telugu మూడు (mūḍu) and Tulu ಮೂಜಿ (mūji).

words.g: four (numeral: ௪)
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *nānk(k)V (“four”). Cognate with Malayalam നാങ്ക് (nāṅkŭ), Kurux नाख़ (nāx), Toda [script needed] (nōng), Kota (India) [script needed] (nāng).

words.g: ten (numeral: ௰)
words.e:
Inherited from Middle Tamil பஃது (paḥtu), from Old Tamil 𑀧𑀂𑀢𑀼 (paḥtu), ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *paHtu (“ten”).
Cognate with Kannada ಹತ್ತು (hattu), Malayalam പത്ത് (pattŭ), Telugu పది (padi), Tulu ಪತ್ತ್ (pattŭ).

words.g: hundred
words.e: From Proto-South Dravidian *nūṯu (“hundred”). Cognate with Kannada ನೂರು (nūru), Malayalam നൂറ് (nūṟŭ), Telugu నూరు (nūru), Tulu ನೂದು (nūdu).

words.g: ocean, sea
words.e: From கட (kaṭa, “to cross, go through”) + அல் (al, “torment, obstacle”, compare அல்லல் (allal)), translates to 'torment/obstacle to cross.' Cognate to Kannada ಕಡಲು (kaḍalu), Malayalam കടൽ (kaṭal, “sea”), Telugu కడలి (kaḍali, “sea”), Tulu ಕಡಲ್ (kaḍalŭ, “sea”).

Borrowed from Sanskrit अग्नि (agni, “fire”). Compare Kannada ಅಗ್ನಿ (agni, “fire”), Malayalam അഗ്നി (agni, “fire”), Telugu అగ్ని (agn…

words.g: deva, god
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *dyew-
Proto-Indo-European *-ós
Proto-Indo-European *deywós
Proto-Indo-Iranian *daywás
Sanskrit देव (deva)
Proto-Dravidian *-anṯu
Tamil -அன் (-aṉ)
Tamil தேவன்
From Sanskrit देव (deva, “god”) + -அன் (-aṉ, masculine marker). Doublet of தெய்வம் (teyvam), தேவி (tēvi),…

words.g: drinking water (water that is suitable or intended for ingestion by humans: potable water)
words.e: From குடி (kuṭi, “to drink”) + நீர் (nīr, “water”).

words.g: the fruit brinjal, eggplant, aubergine (Solanum melongena)
words.e: Compound of கத்தரி (kattari) + காய் (kāy).

words.e: Cognate with Kannada ಮಂಜಳ (mañjaḷa), Kodava ಮಂಜ (mañja), Malayalam മഞ്ഞൾ (maññaḷ), Tulu ಮಂಜಳ್ (mañjaḷŭ). Related to மஞ்சளி (mañcaḷi).

silver (a lustrous, white, metallic element, atomic number 47, atomic weight 107.87, symb…
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *weḷ-i (“silver”); cognate with Kannada ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ (beḷḷi), Malayalam വെള്ളി (veḷḷi), Telugu వెండి (veṇḍi).

words.g: he, that (male) person
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *a-
Tamil அ- (a-)
Tamil -வன் (-vaṉ)
Tamil அவன்
From அ- (a-, distal marker) + -வன் (-vaṉ), see Proto-Dravidian *awanṯu.
Cognates
Cognate with Badaga ಅವ (ava), ಅವನು (avanu), Kannada ಅವನು (avanu), Malayalam അവൻ (avaṉ), Telugu వాడు (vāḍu). False cognate of Taos ą́wąną, ą́…

words.g: a help, hand
words.e:
Inherited from Proto-Dravidian *kay (“hand”).
Cognates
* Gondi కై (kai)
* Kannada ಕೈ (kai)
* Kodava ಕೈ (kay)
* Kolami की (kī)

words.g: pubic hair
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *smoḱru
Sanskrit श्मश्रु (śmaśru)der.
Tamil மயிர்
Derived from Sanskrit ஶ்மஶ்ரு (śmaśru). Doublet of மசிர் (macir). Cognate with Malayalam മയിർ (mayiṟ), മശിർ (maśiṟ).

words.g: short for சர்க்கரை நோய் (carkkarai nōy, “diabetes”)
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱorkeh₂
Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćárkaraH
Proto-Indo-Aryan *śárkaraH
Sanskrit शर्करा (śarkarā)bor.
Tamil சர்க்கரை
From Sanskrit शर्करा (śarkarā).

words.g: one of the names of the Tamil alphasyllabic letter ந (na)
words.e: Compound of ந் (n) + அகரம் (akaram), to mean, 'consonant ந் (n) with the vowel அ (a) sound.'

words.g: gold, pure gold
words.e: Probably borrowed from Sanskrit टङ्क (ṭaṅka). Doublet of டங்கம் (ṭaṅkam). Cognate with Malayalam തങ്കം (taṅkaṁ).

words.g: cold water
words.e:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *taṇ

words.g: of; concerning; about
words.e: Inherited from Proto-Italic *dē (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₁ (“towards”), from *de (“to, towards”) + *-h₁ (instrumental suffix). Also in suffixes -dam, -dum, -de, -dō (e.g. quondam, inde, unde, quandō), dōnec, Ancient Greek δέ (dé), δή (dḗ), English to.
